items.title: Vincent Assafuah petitions CHRAJ to investigate alleged irregularities in 2026 World Cup visa arrangements
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Old Tafo, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, has petitioned the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) to investigate suspected corruption and administrative irregularities in the allocation and management of visa opportunities linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. In a petition on Thursday, October 15, the MP named the National Sports Authority (NSA), the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, alongside private entities including TRIBE Culture Fest and the Ghana Tourism Federation (GHATOF), and called for an independent investigation into their roles. Mr Assafuah is asking CHRAJ to investigate discrepancies in beneficiary lists, the verification of individuals presented as institutional personnel, the selection criteria used to allocate visa opportunities, and the handling of payments and sponsorship proceeds. According to the petition, a list of 102 names submitted in connection with the NSA reportedly contained only 15 individuals who could be verified as personnel through the records examined. The Old Tafo MP said the discrepancy requires an explanation supported by documentary evidence. He has also called for scrutiny of the GTA’s reported allocation of 400 United States visa slots and 800 Canadian slots, including the selection procedures, approvals and use of sponsorship proceeds. The petition cites a reported July 2026 request by 14 GTA regional directors for explanations about the allocation and the utilisation of funds. It further raises concerns over alleged payments of about GH¢2,250 per person under arrangements involving GHATOF, questioning whether visa fees were paid and whether money collected from applicants was refunded. Mr Assafuah has urged CHRAJ to obtain the relevant agreements, correspondence, beneficiary lists and financial records, establish the responsibilities of the institutions and individuals involved, and determine whether any public officer abused their position or breached administrative duties. He stressed that the allegations should not be treated as established findings and asked the Commission to make appropriate recommendations or refer evidence of suspected criminal conduct to the relevant authorities where warranted. The petition invokes Articles 218(a) and 218(e) of the 1992 Constitution and the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice Act, 1993 (Act 456).

items.title: 12-year-old boy found dead in muddy pit at Opeikuma
items.description: A 12-year-old boy has been found dead in a muddy, water-filled pit in a bush behind a building fence at Opeikuma Vat in the Awutu Senya East Municipality of the Central Region, in a suspected murder incident. The boy’s body was reportedly discovered in a bush behind a building fence, hours after he was reportedly involved in a physical altercation with his mother. He was found partially naked, lying in a supine position inside the muddy pit with evident wounds on his body. The cause of the injuries and the circumstances that led to his death have not yet been established. Reports from the area allege that the deceased’s mentally challenged mother has been involved in a string of violence towards him and other members of the community. A resident, Madam Comfort Yaboah, told reporters that Gifty had previously been taken by her family for treatment following concerns about her mental health. The police who were called to the scene arrived promptly to evaluate the area and retrieve the body for preservation. Meanwhile, the family of the victim have declined to speculate and are waiting for the circumstances of the boy’s death to be established through investigation.

items.title: GHS begins Yellow Fever vaccination campaign in three Upper West districts
items.description: The Ghana Health Service has started a Yellow Fever Reactive Vaccination Campaign in the Wa West, Sissala East, and Sissala West districts of the Upper West Region. The exercise commenced on Wednesday, October 14, and is expected to end on Sunday, October 18, 2026. The five-day campaign is aiming to vaccinate approximately 244,869 persons aged nine months to 60 years across the three districts. The primary objective is to halt the spread of the yellow fever outbreak and protect the population against the disease. To ensure wide coverage and easy access to vaccination services, trained health workers have been deployed to health facilities, and temporary vaccination posts have been established at strategic public locations, including markets, bus stations, churches, mosques, schools, and other public areas. Mobile vaccination teams are also visiting settlements, towns, and villages to reach all eligible persons within the campaign areas. All individuals vaccinated during the campaign are being issued yellow vaccination cards as official proof of vaccination. The public is advised to keep these cards safely, as they may be required at health facilities, schools, or during travel. Yellow Fever vaccination remains the most effective means of preventing the disease and controlling outbreaks. A single dose of the vaccine provides lifelong protection, making vaccination a critical intervention in safeguarding individuals and communities against Yellow Fever. The Ghana Health Service strongly encouraged all eligible persons aged nine months to 60 years in the three districts to participate in the campaign and get vaccinated. Public participation is essential to achieving high vaccination coverage, stopping the spread of the outbreak, and protecting the health and well-being of the population.

items.title: Organised Labour pushes for higher 2027 base pay despite slowing inflation
items.description: Organised Labour is pushing for a significant increase in the 2027 base pay, arguing that slowing inflation has not translated into lower market prices or restored workers’ purchasing power. The negotiations come ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget, with government and labour facing pressure to reach an agreement on the new base pay. The current base pay reflects a 9 per cent increase across the Single Spine Salary Structure for January to December 2026. President of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA), Dr Ernest Yorke, says organised labour will make a strong case for an upward adjustment, despite the decline in the rate of inflation. He explained that lower inflation does not necessarily mean goods and services have become cheaper, but rather that prices are increasing at a slower rate. “Inflation may have slowed, which we accept, and that will certainly factor into what our positions would be. But certainly, inflation may have meant that prices of goods and services are the same. Just that the rate of change year on year has slowed,” he said. Dr Yorke noted that workers continue to face high living costs, which have affected their ability to maintain their purchasing power. He said labour would present evidence and reasons to justify its demand for a higher increase during the negotiations. “It’s a dialogue, but then we are reasonable people on the labour side. But I think the government will also be real and accept the fact that things are…” he added. According to him, organised labour is seeking an improved base pay that would translate into better salaries, take-home pay and other emoluments for workers across the country, not only doctors. “We are going to engage and make a forceful argument as to why upward adjustment of our base pay and basic salary and other emoluments are warranted for us,” he said.

items.title: Terrorism: Court jails 2 for life for assisting Boko Haram members
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced two men to life imprisonment for providing support to members of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group. The convicts, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS). Trial Justice Salim Ibrahim handed down the sentence after the duo pleaded guilty to the charge the Federal Government preferred against them. The Federal Government alleged that, aside from aiding the operations of insurgents, the convicts also concealed information about their whereabouts. While they received life imprisonment on the first count of the charge, the court sentenced them to 20 years on the second count. The judgment followed the resumption of another phase of the mass trial of alleged terrorists and their facilitators by the Federal Government. No fewer than 59 suspects were listed to appear before various judges of the court. Some of the judges presiding over the cases include Justices Ibrahim, James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu. It will be recalled that in June, the Federal Government prosecuted over 600 individuals allegedly affiliated with terrorist organisations. The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, said the exercise was meant to send a clear message that the administration is not treating terrorism with levity. items.title: Parliament’s Human Rights Committee demands swift justice in Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse case
items.description: Parliament’s Committee on Human Rights has called for swift justice in the alleged sexual abuse case at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), urging authorities to ensure accountability and strengthen safeguards for students. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 15, the Committee said it had taken note of a JoyNews investigation detailing allegations of sexual abuse at the school and the subsequent suspension of its headmaster, Zakaria Abdulali. The Committee condemned the alleged conduct and said it was monitoring the investigation and prosecution of the case as part of its parliamentary oversight responsibilities. The Committee said the alleged conduct raised concerns under Sections 2 and 13 of Ghana’s Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), as well as Article 34 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, which addresses the protection of children from sexual exploitation and abuse. It urged school authorities, teachers and other staff in second-cycle and other educational institutions to uphold high standards of professional and ethical conduct and protect the rights of children in their care. The Committee said students must be able to pursue their right to education in environments where their safety and dignity are protected. The Committee commended the Minister of Education and the Ghana Education Service (GES) for the steps taken following the allegations, including the suspension of the headmaster and a housemaster and the initiation of a police investigation. It also appealed to the justice system to expedite the handling of the case. The Committee called for the maximum applicable sentence if the headmaster is found guilty, saying this would help deter similar offences. However, the allegations against the suspended headmaster have not been established in court. The case has attracted national attention following reports that the number of students alleging sexual abuse had risen to 16, according to investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The school was temporarily closed after unrest involving students and the destruction of school property. Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the GES to suspend Abdulali pending investigations and requested the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to investigate the allegations. Reports have also linked the suspended headmaster to the National Democratic Congress (NDC), identifying him as the party’s constituency secretary in Juaben and indicating that he had intended to contest the constituency chairmanship. The Committee, chaired by Kumawu Member of Parliament Ernest Yaw Anim, said it would continue monitoring the investigation and prosecution. It also expressed hope that the case would lead to policy reviews and stronger safeguards to protect children in educational institutions across the country. The investigations by the GES and the police remain ongoing.

items.title: L’association « Nous sommes la solution » appelle les Etats à investir sur la femme rurale
items.description: La journée de la femme rurale a mobilisé plusieurs femmes dans la commune de Sédhiou. Cette rencontre tenue ce 15 octobre 2026 a été un prétexte pour la présidente de « Nous sommes la solution », une organisation agroécologique panafricaine, de plaider pour le soutien des activités agricoles des femmes rurales. SEDHIOU- L'ambiance était au rendez-vous ce jeudi 15 octobre, sur la place de l’indépendance de la région de Sédhiou où plusieurs femmes venues de différents horizons ont célébré la journée internationale de la femme rurale. Cette rencontre a permis de mettre en exergue le rôle de la femme dans la production agroécologique. « Si aujourd’hui on parle de l’agroécologie, c’est grâce au travail inlassable des femmes rurales dans l’agriculture vivrière », estime Mariama Sonko, présidente du mouvement panafricain « nous sommes la solution ». Rappelant que cette agroécologie est basée sur le savoir et savoir-faire que les ancêtres ont transmis depuis des générations. La présidente l’association nous sommes la solution a aussi a loué la bravoure et le mérite de la femme rurale. « Aujourd’hui, investir dans cette couche de femme, c’est investir sur l’ensemble de la population africaine », a-t-assumé. Cette année, la journée de la femme rurale est célébrée autour de : « L’émancipation des femmes : construire un avenir résilient avec Beijing+30. Investir dans la femme rurale : un levier pour la croissance économique et le développement durable ». Ce thème est un prétexte, pour Mme Sonko de rappeler la doléance de son association. « Depuis 2011 nous plaidons pour que l’Etat investisse sur cette pratique agroécologie dont détiennent les femmes rurales. Malheureusement, ils sont toujours rués sur l’autre pratique qui détruit notre agriculture », regrette-elle. La santé de l’environnement aussi bien que celle des êtres vivants est menacée par cette forme d’agriculture. L’association « Nous sommes la solution », est présente Bénin, du Burkina Faso, de la Côte d’Ivoire, de la Gambie, du Ghana, de la Guinée, de la Guinée-Bissau, du Mali, de la Mauritanie, du Niger, du Sénégal et du Togo. Elle réunit en son sein 800 associations de femmes rurales regroupant plus de 200 000 membres et sympathisants. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (correspondant)

items.title: This Is Edgar Allan Poe and I Am Begging Kelly Clarkson to Take My Bird
items.description: Dear Kelly Clarkson, Miss Clarkson. I have read that you wanted a bird but were not permitted to obtain it. Well, I am in possession of a bird and do not want to be. Perhaps we could come to a mutually beneficial arrangement. In brief: There is a bird in here. Specifically, a raven. It sits, croaking, uninvited, on my bust of Pallas. (I would also be happy to give you the bust of Pallas. It is a tasteful bust; my only qualm with it is that it reminds me of my lost Lenore.) I didn’t ask the bird to be here. To the contrary, I would like nothing more than for it to depart. I have asked it to do so, first politely, and then rudely. But nothing. The raven will not budge. When I read of your encounter with the store Art of Play I felt the only hint of hope I had felt for quite some time. I thought: This woman needs a bird. I have a bird. I will tell her the situation, and we can wring some triumph out of this whole miserable thing. How did I come by this bird? Oh, the usual way. I’m sure you know the feeling. It’s a midnight dreary. You’re pondering, weak and weary, many and many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore. You are thinking of your lost Lenore. Then you hear a tapping, as of someone gently rapping, rapping at your chamber door? Well, this happened to me recently. But it wasn’t someone. It was a bird. And now the accursed thing will not depart! I want to be rid of the bird. And you want a bird. I understand that the bird in which you expressed interest is a windup bird. Well, this raven certainly winds me up. Is that anything? I understand that the bird in which you were interested is named Molly. My raven could be named Molly. You could call it anything if only you would take the demonic thing out of here! Before you object that the kind of bird you want is inanimate, whereas mine is clearly a live bird, I have considered this, and I think that the main objection people have to a live bird indoors is that the bird will fly around disruptively and try to escape. Well, the raven does not do that. I wish it would. I have opened the casement. I have said, “Shoo, bird.” I have said sterner things, things that I now regret. But the raven does not budge. It just sits there and says, “Nevermore,” at intervals. Also, its sable hue would go with anything. Looking at this bird from an interior-design perspective, I think it would fit any room, especially if I included the bust, which, again, I am willing to do. Do you need to feed it? I have not gotten that far with the bird. So far, it has not eaten anything. I think maybe it sustains itself by other means. It just sits there saying, “Nevermore.” Make no mistake, I am not offering you a free bird because I doubt your ability to pay. I am offering you a bird because I hate the infernal creature and want it out of my sight! But I would accept your money. Using that money, I could perhaps even get rid of the beating heart that seems to be stuck in my wall. I eagerly await your response. Sincerely, EAP

items.title: JOJ « DAKAR 2026 »: Finitions, budget, héritage… Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye lève le voile
items.description: À deux semaines de l’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, prévue le 31 octobre à 17 heures à Diamniadio, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, président du comité d’organisation, a détaillé dans un entretien avec Le Soleil à paraître ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 dans l’édition print, l’état des préparatifs, le financement et les ambitions de ces premiers Joj organisés en Afrique. Dans quinze jours, sera donné le coup d’envoi des Joj Dakar 2026. L’heure n’est plus donc aux grands chantiers, mais aux finitions. C’est le message central livré par le président du Comité d’organisation des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (Cojoj), Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, dans une interview exclusive à lire dans la version papier du Soleil de ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Évaluant l'état d'avancement général à 92 %, il insiste sur une « confiance active » pour régler le « dernier kilomètre » : la synchronisation des transports, l'accréditation des volontaires, la logistique et l'approvisionnement en eau sur tous les sites. « Le 31 octobre à 17 heures, à Diamniadio, le Sénégal accueillera le monde. Nous ne promettons pas des Jeux parfaits, mais des Jeux authentiques, à la hauteur de la Téranga sénégalaise », a laissé entendre le président du Cnoss. Interrogé sur la remise récente de plusieurs infrastructures clés par le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye y voit un acte fort de souveraineté nationale. Le Village des Jeux à Diamniadio, le stade Iba-Mar-Diop rénové ou encore la piscine olympique intègrent désormais le patrimoine pérenne du pays. Pour éviter le piège des « éléphants blancs », le Cojoj, selon lui, s'est aligné sur les exigences de sobriété et de durabilité du Comité international olympique (Cio). C’est-à-dire sobriété et réhabilitation (à Diamniadio, le Cojoj a privilégié la rénovation à la construction neuve) ; reconversion garantie (le Village des Jeux deviendra un campus universitaire dès la fin de la compétition) et modèle économique (l’entretien des sites est confié à l’Agence de gestion du patrimoine bâti, avec des crédits d'ores et déjà provisionnés dans la loi de finances). Un budget présenté comme sécurisé et public Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye affirme que le budget est sécurisé à 100 % et public. Il dément les chiffres de 80 milliards de Fcfa avancés par certains. Il précise que le budget opérationnel du Cojoj s’élève à 32 milliards de Fcfa, financés à 60 % par le Cio et ses partenaires. Le reste correspond aux investissements de l’État (routes, eau, stades), qui resteront au pays. Bien que les compétitions soient concentrées entre Dakar, Diamniadio et Saly, l’événement se veut national. Le Cojoj a déployé un vaste dispositif d'animation territoriale impliquant 45 collectivités, 300 associations Navétanes et 12 000 écoles, appuyé par une billetterie accessible à 1 000 FCFA pour les clubs et scolaires. La tournée de la flamme olympique à travers les capitales régionales – portée par des figures du sport sénégalais comme Brancou Badio, Oumy Diop, Louis François Mendy, Fary Seye ou Ousseynou Diop – a confirmé l'engouement populaire. L’Afrique au cœur du mouvement olympique Pendant 130 ans, l'Afrique est restée spectatrice des Jeux. Pour Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, la responsabilité confiée au Sénégal dépasse largement ses frontières : il s'agit d'organiser l'événement au nom des 54 pays du continent. Le succès de Dakar 2026 doit ouvrir la voie à de futures candidatures africaines pour les Jeux Olympiques de 2036 ou 2040, estime-t-il. Sur le plan sportif et humain, la dimension continentale s'incarne directement. Sur le terrain, plus de 800 athlètes africains prendront part aux épreuves. Dans l'organisation, 400 jeunes professionnels issus de 30 pays africains sont intégrés au sein de la Learning Academy, véritable cœur de transmission des compétences d'organisation événementielle. Pour le président du Cojoj, au-delà des médailles, l'objectif affiché est de susciter des vocations et de multiplier par trois l'accès des jeunes sénégalais à des infrastructures sportives modernes. Pour mesurer l'impact réel à long terme, un Observatoire de l’Héritage a été mis en place en collaboration avec l’Ansd et l’Ucad, afin d'évaluer chaque année le taux d'utilisation des sites, le nombre de licenciés et la formation des jeunes. Revenant sur le report des Jeux en 2020 dû à la pandémie de Covid-19 – un moment perçu initialement comme un coup dur -, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye conclut qu'il s'est transformé en opportunité pour parfaire l'organisation. Son invitation finale s'adresse directement au public : « Venez le 31 octobre. Ne regardez pas Dakar 2026 à la télévision : vivez ces Jeux ! » Par Elhadj Ibrahima THIAM et Samba Oumar FALL Retrouvez l’intégralité de cet entretien dans Le Soleil du vendredi 16 octobre 2026.

items.title: Senate orders probe into corps member’s death at Enugu NYSC camp
items.description: The Senate has ordered an investigation into the death of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member, Etimbuk Daniel, at the Enugu State orientation camp, amid concerns over medical facilities and emergency response services in camps nationwide. The resolution, adopted on Thursday, followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Aniekan Bassey, who called for an urgent review of healthcare services available to corps members across the country. The investigation will be conducted by the Senate Committees on Police Affairs, Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, Youth Development and Health, in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services. The probe is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding Daniel’s death and determine whether any lapses occurred in the provision of medical care at the camp. Bassey expressed concern over “the sudden and untimely passing of the corps member, describing him as a vibrant, patriotic young Nigerian and a shining light of his community who had only set out to serve the country.” He said the incident raised broader questions about the adequacy of medical services available to corps members participating in the mandatory national service programme. “The incident is not isolated, but highlights a recurring pattern of systemic negligence, poor medical infrastructure, and absence of qualified emergency personnel and rapid referral protocols across NYSC camps, underlining that the government owes a duty of care to young graduates mobilized away from their homes to serve the nation.” The senator said Daniel had embarked on national service with hopes of contributing to Nigeria’s development before his death. He called for urgent legislative scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly allegations of medical negligence, inadequate healthcare infrastructure and ineffective emergency response and referral systems at orientation camps. Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Bassey said the security and welfare of the people remained the primary purpose of government. He argued that the government and relevant authorities had a responsibility to protect corps members and ensure they received timely and adequate medical care throughout their service year. Bassey added that Daniel’s death had thrown his family, associates, the student community and the people of Akwa Ibom State into mourning, stressing the need for a thorough investigation. The Senate Chief Whip, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North, seconded the motion. Contributing to the debate, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, expressed condolences to Daniel’s family, Bassey and the people of Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria. Ningi urged the relevant committees to make concrete recommendations and identify measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. The Senate subsequently observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased. Daniel, the immediate past Students’ Union Government president of Akwa Ibom State University, reportedly died at the NYSC orientation camp in Enugu State following allegations that he was given fake medication and did not receive timely medical attention. Reports indicated that Daniel complained of a headache at the camp and was given medication, but his condition allegedly deteriorated afterwards. items.title: 50 houses razed, scores injured as explosion rocks Rivers community
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor About 20 people have been injured and over 50 houses burnt down following the explosion of a gas pipeline in Aleto community, Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State. The incident, which happened Thursday, occurred around 5pm occured from an alleged ruptured pipeline belonging to the Nigeria Gas Company along the Old Bori Road in Aleto. A source, who is a resident of the area, narrated: “The Pipeline has caused injuries and damaged properties. This pipeline has been leaking for about three weeks before the explosion today.” The source gave his name as Emmanuel said some leaders of the area have notified the company about the leak but the company did not respond positively. Leader of the Eleme Legislative Council, Daniel Chuma, said he had written to the company about the leak and followed up with a petition to relevant authorities but nothing concrete was done to stop the gas leak. Chuma, who visited the scene of the explosion, said: “There was a leakage on another section of the Nigeria Gas Company. We wrote to them, and we did a petition to NOSDRA and Rivers State Ministry of Environment and copied the Police for urgent intervention. “We asked for a joint investigation. We don’t know what they did before they left. Today we were called to an explosion at the same pipeline of the Nigeria Gas Company that has destroyed over 50 houses, cars, and many casualties. People have been rushed to the hospital. “Before now, everyone scampered for safety. The few that came, we asked them to stay far away to avoid any further incident.” Meanwhile, the Executive Director of the Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre, YEAC-Nigeria, Dr Fyneface Dumnamene, in a statement, confirmed the development. Fyneface said: “We are using this medium to call on the relevant authorities, the Rivers State government, Ministry of Environment, NOSDRA, the Rivers State, the Federal Government, and all the bodies involved in checking oil spill and explosion to come to the aid of Aleto people. This is a serious incident. “As of the time of this statement, YEAC-Nigeria has not independently confirmed any fatalities. “Members of the Advocacy Centre’s volunteers who visited the scene for independent verification confirmed the presence of officials of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on ground. The cause of the incident is yet to be independently verified. “YEAC-Nigeria calls on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) to identify the facility operator and conduct a Joint Investigation Visit to the site, and to invoke relevant provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021 as appropriate,” he added. The post 50 houses razed, scores injured as explosion rocks Rivers community appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu ordered security chiefs to guarantee safe elections — Defence Minister
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has directed heads of security agencies to ensure a safe and secure environment for Nigerians to vote freely in the elections scheduled for January, Minister of Defence General Christopher Musa (retd) has said. The minister disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents after a security meeting presided over by the President at Aso Villa, Abuja. He said the session was convened to update Tinubu on the security situation across the country ahead of the polls. “Today’s meeting was to brief Mr. President on the security situation within the country. You know, the elections coming in January, and it’s important that we keep him abreast of what is ongoing,” the minister said. Gen. Musa said all heads of security agencies attended the “intensive discussion,” during which the President made clear his expectation for the electoral process. “Mr. President made it very clear he wants a free, fair, and credible election. We must do everything possible to ensure that the country is safe and secure for the citizens to go out and vote,” Musa stated. The minister assured Nigerians that the security forces would remain neutral and would not allow intimidation of voters or political actors. “We are going to ensure that we give everybody opportunity to go and serve, so they have nothing to worry about, nothing to be afraid of, and that nobody is going to intimidate them for whatever reasons,” he said. “It is important for all other political parties to ensure to understand that the security forces are going to be neutral.” The Defence Minister also dismissed suggestions that underage persons were being recruited into the armed forces, saying the concern related to terrorists’ use of children. According to him, “There is nobody that is underage that is being brought here. I think the discussion that was made was that the accusation was on the terrorists using underage. “Well, we know that we don’t have control over what they do, and that’s why it’s important for us to understand that we must not allow them remain wherever they are.” He said the President had ordered security agencies to intensify operations to locate abducted persons and dismantle terrorist and bandit enclaves. “The directive from the president is: all of us must go all out to fish out and rescue all those that have been abducted, kidnapped wherever they are. There shouldn’t be any camp of any terrorists or bandits anywhere in Nigeria,” Musa declared. On measures to improve security capacity, the minister cited increased recruitment, training, and procurement. He said the President would soon commission “almost about 10” newly acquired aircraft and helicopters. “Mr. President is coming to commission a set of new aircrafts and helicopters that have been bought. I think almost about 10 of them in number, and to show Nigerians that despite the economic issue, the issue of security is in the front burner of Mr. President’s view,” he said. The minister also pointed to the recent salary increment for members of the armed forces, adding that improvements for the police, other agencies, and pensioners were being addressed. “I’m sure very soon the police and all others is being been addressed, including those of the pensioners. Nobody is going to be left behind,” he said. The minister urged citizens to support security agencies by reporting wrongdoing, including misconduct by security personnel. “Security is everybody’s responsibility. It’s not only for members of security forces. Everyone has a role to play,” he said. “Whatever you see that is going wrong, even with our members that are not doing what is right, please don’t hesitate to report. Action will be taken.” The high-level meeting was attended by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Minister of Police Affairs, Senator Ibrahim Gaidam; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; and Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka Famadewa (rtd.). Also in attendance were the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu; Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas; Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke; and Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Undiandeye. Other security chiefs at the meeting included the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu; Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency (NIA), Ambassador Mohammed Mohammed; and Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi. The post Tinubu ordered security chiefs to guarantee safe elections — Defence Minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: From Campaign Propaganda to Gov’t Accountability: When the message-makers demand a seat at the table
items.description: The campaign is over, the votes have been counted, and power has changed hands. But what happens when the very voices that helped sell a political message begin demanding answers from the government they helped bring to power? Ghana may be witnessing one of the most fascinating consequences of modern political communication: the struggle between those who shape the message and those who must ultimately govern. THE THEATRE OF GHANA’S 2024 ELECTIONS Ghana’s 2024 general elections now belong to history, but the dramatic scenes that defined the campaign remain memorable. The National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, John Dramani Mahama, popularised the emphatic slogan, “NDC, no turning back,” while the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, used the metaphor of a driver seeking the keys to lead Ghana forward. These campaign performances were more than political entertainment. They were communication strategies designed to make messages memorable, build emotional connections and persuade voters. Both candidates and their supporters made extensive use of social media to reach eligible voters. The Electoral Commission declared Mahama the winner of the December 2024 presidential election, with Bawumia conceding defeat. The electorate had made its choice. Reuters’ election report . But the end of a campaign does not necessarily end the influence of those who helped shape it. BERNAYS AND THE POWER BEHIND PUBLIC OPINION In his 1928 book Propaganda , public relations pioneer Edward L. Bernays made a provocative observation about the power of persuasion in democratic society. He wrote: “The conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organised habits and opinions of the masses is an important element in democratic society.” Bernays went further, arguing that those who influence public opinion can constitute an “invisible government” because they help shape how people think, what they value and how they respond to public issues . Bernays, 1928, p. 9 This idea offers a useful lens through which to examine modern political campaigns in Ghana. Political communication is not simply about presenting policies. It is also about deciding which issues receive attention, how problems are framed, which emotions are activated and which political narratives become dominant. During the 2024 campaign, NDC communicators and activists repeatedly criticised the record of the then governing NPP. Their messaging formed part of a wider contest over economic hardship, public confidence, accountability and the direction of the country. In my view, the effectiveness of the NDC’s campaign communication deserves examination. However, it would be simplistic to attribute the election result to propaganda alone. Economic conditions, voters’ experiences, policy choices, party organisation and many other factors also shaped the outcome. The important question is what happens when the campaign machinery continues operating after the election. WHEN THE CAMPAIGN PROMISES BECOME THE PUBLIC’S SCORECARD Among the commitments Mahama made during the campaign was a proposal to drill boreholes on cocoa farms and provide water-storage facilities to help farmers irrigate their farms during dry periods. MyJoyOnline reported the proposal in November 2024 The NDC also campaigned on a 24-hour economy, built around three eight-hour shifts intended to increase productivity and create employment. These were campaign commitments, not merely slogans. They created expectations among citizens who hoped to see tangible improvements in employment, agriculture and living standards. Whether individual promises have been fulfilled, partially implemented, delayed or remain outstanding must be assessed through current evidence, official implementation records and the experiences of the intended beneficiaries. But one principle is beyond dispute: “a campaign promise does not become a government achievement simply because it was repeated convincingly during an election.” It must be measured against what is actually delivered. This is where citizen journalists, bloggers and content creators become particularly important. They can visit communities, interview farmers, speak to unemployed young people, document unfinished projects and ask questions that may not receive sustained attention in traditional newsrooms. Their work can help transform campaign rhetoric into public scrutiny. THE PROPAGANDIST IS NOT THE PRESIDENT Here lies the central dilemma. When political activists spend months promoting a candidate, defending campaign messages and challenging opponents, some may come to regard themselves as indispensable to the political victory. They may expect access, influence or recognition once their preferred candidate takes office. That possibility deserves attention, but it should not be assumed that every supporter expects a position or that every online critic once served as a campaign propagandist. The broader question is whether political communication can create expectations that become difficult to manage after an election. A campaign requires persuasion. Government requires administration, evidence, negotiation, public accountability and decisions that must be judged by their results. Those are different responsibilities. The people who helped communicate a party’s message do not automatically acquire authority over government decisions. Equally, winning an election does not give a president the right to disregard citizens who helped build public support or who now question the administration’s performance. The citizen is not a campaign prop, and the content creator is not a permanent public-relations officer for the party he or she supported. Once the votes are counted, the relationship must change. Supporters, critics and undecided citizens all retain the right to demand answers. FROM PROPAGANDA TO ACCOUNTABILITY I do not believe Bernays’s argument means that the public is powerless or that a small group can control every political outcome. People can question messages, compare competing accounts, reject political claims and change their minds when presented with evidence. That is why the rise of citizen journalism matters. A viral video is not automatically proof. A trending allegation is not a verified fact. Bloggers and content creators must distinguish evidence from speculation, correct errors and give people accused of wrongdoing a fair opportunity to respond. Governments, meanwhile, should not dismiss legitimate criticism merely because it arrives through Facebook, TikTok, YouTube or WhatsApp. Where allegations concern public spending, campaign promises or possible wrongdoing, the appropriate response is to examine the evidence, provide clear explanations and allow lawful accountability processes to operate. The media’s responsibility is to investigate. The citizen’s responsibility is to question. The government’s responsibility is to account for its decisions. GHANA MUST MOVE BEYOND CAMPAIGN THEATRE The 2024 election demonstrated the importance of political storytelling and digital communication. But the real test of democracy begins after the rallies, slogans, campaign videos and victory celebrations have ended. Bernays helps us understand how public opinion can be shaped. Ghana’s democratic experience must also remind us that public opinion can change, and those who once helped promote a political message can later become among its most determined questioners. The lesson is not that propaganda alone wins elections or that every campaign activist seeks to control government. It is that political communication creates expectations, and those expectations must eventually confront reality. President Mahama’s administration should be assessed by its documented actions and results, not simply by the strength of its campaign messaging. The same standard should apply to every government. And citizen journalists, bloggers and content creators should understand that their greatest public service is not to protect a political party from embarrassment, but to help citizens establish what is true, what remains unfulfilled and what must be done. The campaign may end on election day, but accountability has no closing date. In Ghana’s democracy, the microphone belongs to the people. Those who once used it to help a candidate win must remain free to use it to ask what happens next. That is not betrayal. It is part of the democratic responsibility that begins when the campaign ends.

items.title: Abusive Care Facility in Thailand Raises Broader Concerns
items.description: Click to expand Image A person lies in bed at a nursing home in Ayutthaya, Thailand, April 9, 2016. © 2016 Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters A care facility in Kanchanaburi, Thailand made headlines in early October when photos of conditions in the facility went viral, including images allegedly depicting metal cages that confine residents to their beds. Further investigation by the country’s Department of Health Service Support uncovered unsanitary conditions and overcrowding, as well as evidence that the facility had been treating residents with psychosocial disabilities (mental health conditions) without an appropriate license. The whistleblower, known as “Mae Phat,” appeared on television to recount her experiences at Sothornchai Nursing Home as a former resident, describing how she was involuntarily committed, forced to take medication, and physically restrained, often for hours at a time. Thai officials promptly ordered the facility’s closure as well as inspections of 1,203 facilities for older people nationwide. While the authorities have taken appropriate first steps, conditions at the facility have raised broader concerns about institutionalization, shackling, and the treatment of older people in Thailand. The United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs predicts that 28 percent of Thailand's population will be 65 or older within the next decade. Though Thailand has launched a community-based long-term care program for older people, responsibility for care falls under several government ministries. Ongoing shortages of qualified care and support workers as well as budgetary constraints leave many older people reliant on family care, which not all families can adequately provide. The Thai government should take this opportunity to reconsider its fragmented policies and commit to ensuring older people are treated with dignity and empowered to make decisions about their care and support. The government should develop and implement a comprehensive, time-bound deinstitutionalization plan for older people and people with disabilities, ensuring full access to community-based services and individualized support that would enable them to live independently and participate fully in their communities. The government should also establish a task force to conduct regular, unannounced visits to public and private institutions housing older people and people with psychosocial disabilities, assessing living conditions and conducting confidential interviews with residents and staff. This task force should also establish a hotline to receive and investigate reports of abuse and ensure accountability. Thailand should move beyond institutional care and guarantee everyone the support required to live independently in the community.

items.title: ‘He slipped, knocked head in bathroom’ – Ningi recounts Senator Mandiya’s death
items.description: The Senator representing Bauchi Central, Abdul Ningi, has recounted the circumstances surrounding the death of his late colleague, Bello Mandiya, who reportedly slipped and hit his head in his bathroom, with his body discovered about 72 hours later at his Abuja residence. Ningi narrated the incident during Senate plenary on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. A video of his account went viral on Thursday. According to Ningi, Mandiya lived alone, and his absence went unnoticed for days until the chief imam of Apo became concerned that the former lawmaker had missed prayers for three consecutive days. Ningi said he was in Saudi Arabia when his son called to inform him of Mandiya’s death. His son was among those who discovered the former senator’s body on September 7, 2026. Recounting the events leading to the discovery, Ningi said Mandiya was last seen by a colleague at about 11 am on Friday, September 4, after returning home to prepare for the congregational prayer. “He brought out his cap, his phones, and put them on the bed, and went into the bathroom to take his bath. “After taking his bath, when he was out of the bathroom, then he slipped and knocked his head in the bathroom,” Ningi said. The senator explained that the incident remained unknown until a foul smell began emanating from Mandiya’s apartment, raising concerns among residents. “For 72 hours, Mr President, nobody knew where Bello Mandiya was,” he said. Ningi said those who went to the residence eventually forced the door open and found the former lawmaker dead in the bathroom. “And there lies Bello Mandiya in the bathroom, lifeless. Seventy-two hours, and that’s a simple tragedy,” he said. Reflecting on the incident, Ningi said Mandiya’s death underscored the uncertainty of life, stressing that political positions and material wealth offered no guarantee against tragedy. “There is nothing permanent about anything. Nothing permanent about our position, nothing permanent about our wealth,” Ningi said. The senator, who said he had known Mandiya since 2002, offered prayers for the deceased and extended his condolences to his family, the people of Katsina State and his former constituents. items.title: Ashanti Region Security Coordinator warns sand winners to stay off Accra–Kumasi Expressway site
items.description: Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator, Captain John Kwame Jabari, has warned sand winners operating along the Accra–Kumasi Expressway project site to stop their activities or face severe consequences. He said security personnel had been deployed to the area to prevent further illegal sand winning and protect the planned infrastructure project from disruptions. Speaking on Accra-based Channel One on Thursday, October 15, 2026, Captain Jabari said preliminary investigations suggested that the alleged activities had been ongoing for about two weeks, with operators reportedly entering the area at night with trucks to load sand. “A team has been set up to conduct patrols along the expressway to prevent future incidents or any other offences that may occur along that route. “So, I would like to tell Ghanaians, particularly sand winners, to stay off the expressway. It is a big project that this government wants to embark on, and we are not going to entertain anybody who wants to disrupt the progress of that work,” he said. The warning follows the arrest of 15 men suspected of engaging in sand-winning activities along the expressway project site. The suspects were arrested on Wednesday, October 14, during a security operation in the Sewua–Donyina–Appiadu enclave in the Ashanti Region. Six vehicles, including a wheel loader, were also impounded during the operation. Read also: 15 arrested over alleged sand-winning activities along new Accra-Kumasi Expressway project Assistant Liaison Officer Ivan Bilson Yeboah said the suspects had been transported to the National Security headquarters in Accra for custody and further investigations. Captain Jabari said security personnel would maintain a strong presence along the route to prevent a recurrence and ensure that the project proceeded without interference. “We are going to pay key attention to that route over there. So I like to tell Ghanaians or sand winners that they should stay off the expressway,” he cautioned. He reiterated that authorities would not tolerate activities that could undermine the progress of the expressway project and assured the public that security teams would take action against anyone found engaging in unlawful activities in the area.

items.title: Rebondissement dans l’affaire Dr Diané : Charles Wright se pourvoit en cassation contre l’arrêt en appel
items.description: La bataille judiciaire entre le parquet spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) et l’ancien ministre de la Défense nationale, Dr Mohamed Diané, est loin d’être terminée. Le procureur spécial, Alphonse Charles Wright, a annoncé son intention de se pourvoir en cassation contre l’arrêt rendu par la chambre des appels, dont il conteste les motifs juridiques. Face à la presse, le chef du parquet spécial a indiqué que cette démarche ne visait pas la personne de l’ancien ministre, mais plutôt ce qu’il considère comme une mauvaise interprétation du droit par les magistrats ayant rendu la décision. « Le parquet est formellement en pourvoi contre l’arrêt qui vient d’être rendu par la chambre des appels de la CRIEF. Cette décision, ce n’est pas contre la personne de Dr Diané, c’est la mauvaise interprétation du droit qui a été faite », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, la contestation porte essentiellement sur le raisonnement juridique ayant conduit à cet arrêt. Il entend ainsi soumettre les arguments du ministère public à l’appréciation de la Cour suprême. Revenant sur la procédure, le procureur spécial a rappelé que Dr Diané avait été reconnu coupable en première instance de détournement de deniers publics, d’enrichissement illicite et de blanchiment de capitaux. Il a notamment insisté sur la responsabilité des gestionnaires publics dans la justification de l’utilisation des fonds mis à leur disposition. « Il revient à l’ordonnateur des dépenses de justifier l’exécution de ses dépenses », a-t-il soutenu, estimant que l’ancien ministre n’aurait pas apporté les justifications nécessaires concernant l’utilisation des fonds publics concernés. Le procureur spécial a également soulevé des interrogations sur l’appréciation des faits liés à la commande publique, notamment sur la portée du procès-verbal de réception dans l’examen des éventuelles irrégularités. « Comment peut-on dire que les règles du marché public n’ont pas été violées, par le seul motif qu’il y ait un procès-verbal de réception ? », a-t-il lancé, estimant que l’existence d’un tel document ne saurait, à elle seule, suffire à écarter d’éventuels manquements aux règles de passation des marchés publics. Dans son intervention, Alphonse Charles Wright a, par ailleurs, insisté sur l’obligation de rendre compte qui incombe aux gestionnaires des deniers publics. Il a rappelé que le ministère public avait pour mission de défendre les intérêts de la société guinéenne, tout en veillant au respect des droits des personnes poursuivies devant la juridiction. Le chef du parquet spécial a toutefois réaffirmé son désaccord avec les motifs retenus par la chambre des appels. « Je ne discute pas ce qui a été dit, mais je conteste les motifs légaux qui ont été avancés. […] Je ne peux être convaincu ni par la teneur ni par la forme selon laquelle cette décision a été rendue », a-t-il affirmé. En conclusion, Alphonse Charles Wright a prévenu que le différend judiciaire avec l’ancien ministre était loin d’être clos. « Dr Diané doit savoir que la bataille avec le parquet n’est pas terminée et c’est loin de finir », a-t-il averti. Le pourvoi annoncé ouvre ainsi une nouvelle étape dans cette affaire. Il reviendra désormais à la Cour suprême d’examiner les moyens de droit soulevés par le parquet spécial contre l’arrêt de la chambre des appels de la CRIEF.

items.title: ONU : le Maroc vote pour une résolution soutenant l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui
items.description: Nouvelle grande victoire pour la cause sahraouie devant les institutions internationales. La quatrième commission de l’Assemblée générale de l’ ONU a adopté ce jeudi 15 octobre un projet de résolution sur la question du Sahara occidental, réaffirmant le droit inaliénable du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes onusiens relatifs à la décolonisation. La résolution a été votée également par la délégation marocaine, rapporte l’agence APS . Réaffirmation du caractère de question de décolonisation du conflit sahraoui Cette adoption équivaut à la réaffirmation du caractère de « question de décolonisation inachevée » du conflit sahraoui. Le projet de résolution a été adopté à une écrasante majorité. Il a été examiné dans le cadre des travaux de la commission chargée des questions politiques spéciales et de la décolonisation. La résolution réaffirme le droit inaliénable du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes consacrés par la Charte des Nations unies et aux résolutions pertinentes de l’Assemblée générale, notamment la résolution 1514 du 14 décembre 1960 portant Déclaration sur l’octroi de l’indépendance aux pays et aux peuples coloniaux. Cette adoption « consacre le cadre onusien de la question du Sahara occidental en tant que question de décolonisation inachevée, nécessitant de permettre au peuple sahraoui d’exercer son droit à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes du droit international et aux résolutions pertinentes des Nations unies », écrit l’ APS . Lâché par ses alliés, le Maroc a voté « oui » Selon la même source, le vote a recueilli le soutien de 152 États membres, ce qui souligne « l’importance du respect de la légalité internationale et des engagements des Nations unies en matière de décolonisation, ainsi que le rejet de toute approche susceptible de contourner le droit fondamental des peuples sous domination coloniale à choisir librement leur avenir politique ». L’occupant marocain a lui-même été contraint de voter en faveur du projet de résolution, alors que sa délégation envisageait initialement de s’abstenir de participer au vote. « Face à l’ampleur du soutien exprimé par les États membres, y compris certains de ses alliés, le Maroc a finalement rejoint les voix favorables au texte », indique l’ APS. Après le vote, un responsable du Front Polisario a estimé que la réaffirmation du cadre juridique du Sahara occidental en tant que question de décolonisation constitue une réponse « forte et claire » aux tentatives de l’occupant marocain de déformer la nature juridique de la question sahraouie. Une réponse « forte et claire » au Maroc Sidi Mohamed Ammar, représentant du Front Polisario auprès de l’ONU et coordonnateur avec la MINURSO, a dénoncé, dans une déclaration aux médias, les tentatives du Maroc visant à promouvoir des allégations trompeuses devant la quatrième commission de l’Assemblée générale, en mobilisant un groupe de mercenaires et d’agents pour relayer sa propagande mensongère, ainsi que le recours à l’intimidation verbale au sein de cette instance onusienne. Dans un autre registre, le groupe de Genève de soutien au Sahara occidental a appelé, lors de la 77e session du Comité exécutif du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), à la nécessité de parvenir à « une solution politique juste et durable au conflit du Sahara occidental, conformément aux buts et principes de la Charte des Nations unies ». Cet appel est intervenu dans un communiqué lu par le représentant permanent du Mozambique auprès du bureau des Nations unies à Genève, Geraldo Gonçalves Miguel, au nom du groupe, qui réunit un nombre important de pays africains, asiatiques et d’Amérique latine soutenant le droit du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination. L’article ONU : le Maroc vote pour une résolution soutenant l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Trafic de migrants et traite humaine: 1.597 réseaux criminels démantelés entre 2021 et 2025
items.description: Quelque 1.597 réseaux criminels de trafic de migrants et de traite des êtres humains ont été démantelés entre 2021 et 2025, a indiqué, jeudi à Rabat, le directeur des Affaires pénales, des grâces et de l’observation de la criminalité au ministère de la Justice, président-coordonnateur de la Commission nationale de coordination des mesures de lutte et de prévention de la traite des êtres humains (CNCLT), Hicham Mellati. Présentant le rapport national sur « les efforts du Royaume du Maroc en matière de lutte contre la traite des êtres humains et de prévention » , M. Mellati a fait état de 536 affaires liées à la traite des êtres humains au cours de la période allant de 2021 à 2025, précisant que des poursuites ont été engagées contre 816 personnes, alors que 774 autres ont été condamnées. Le nombre total des victimes officiellement identifiées s'est chiffré, quant à lui, à 988 durant la même période. Cette période a été marquée par des changements structurels profonds et continus dans le dispositif national de lutte et de prévention contre la traite des êtres humains, a-t-il fait valoir, soulignant que ce processus a débuté par la phase de consécration des structures institutionnelles et d'intensification de la coopération technique internationale (2021-2022), avant de franchir une étape charnière marquée par l'adoption du Plan national de lutte contre la traite des êtres humains (2023-2030) et de son plan stratégique de mise en œuvre (2023-2026). Mellati a, de même, fait observer que le rapport présente un bilan de cinq ans reflétant l'interconnexion entre les différentes facettes de la riposte nationale, notant que des avancées multiples ont été enregistrées en matière de lutte contre ce crime à la nature complexe. Pour sa part, Aicha El Iklil, magistrate rattachée à la présidence du Ministère public (PMP) et chef de l'Unité du suivi des affaires de la traite des êtres humains, a mis en avant les efforts déployés par la PMP, en tant que membre de la CNCLT, précisant que ces efforts sont axés sur le renforcement des compétences des magistrats du ministère public, notamment ceux qui sont spécialisés dans lesdites affaires, à travers des formations pointues et des visites de terrain dans les pays aux expériences avérées dans ce domaine. Dans une déclaration à la presse, la Magistrate a noté que la PMP œuvre à l'élaboration d'un guide pratique sur le crime de la traite des êtres humains, qui sera publié prochainement, s'ajoutant à celui relatif aux indicateurs d’identification des enfants victimes de traite. De son côté, Abdelouahed Al Atir, représentant de la Délégation interministérielle aux droits de l'Homme, a indiqué que ce rapport, qui représente une étape importante dans la lutte engagée contre la traite des êtres humains, jette la lumière sur les efforts déployés dans le respect des engagements internationaux y afférents. Pour lui, ce parcours renseigne sur l'engagement sans faille du Maroc à lutter contre ce phénomène et à prendre les mesures nécessaires pour surmonter ses répercussions et son impact. Ce rapport s'inscrit dans le cadre des compétences dévolues à la Commission nationale de coordination des mesures de lutte et de prévention de la traite des êtres humains, en vertu de l'article 7 de la loi N°27.14 relative à la lutte contre ce crime. Il intervient également en réponse aux engagements internationaux du Royaume, au premier rang desquels le Protocole de Palerme additionnel à la Convention des Nations Unies contre la criminalité transnationale organisée, et le mécanisme d'examen de l'application de cette Convention et des protocoles y afférents. Composé de 142 pages, le rapport s'articule autour d'un volet introductif jetant la lumière sur le cadre juridique et institutionnel de la lutte et de la prévention contre la traite des êtres humains, et de cinq axes comprenant « la prévention et la sensibilisation », « les poursuites et la répression judiciaire », « la protection des victimes », « les partenariats et la coopération internationale », et « la formation et le renforcement des capacités », outre une annexe statistique. items.title: La dura negociación sobre el presupuesto de la UE amenaza el acuerdo antes del superaño electoral en Europa
items.description: La pelea sobre el presupuesto que va a marcar las políticas de la UE en los próximos siete años se está encarnizando . Las discrepancias entre los llamados frugales, con Alemania a la cabeza, que abogan por el tijeretazo, y los amigos de la cohesión , entre ellos, España e Italia, que piden más dinero, amenazan con encallar un acuerdo sobre el marco financiero plurianual antes de final de año. Todo ello, en un clima políticamente muy tenso y en vísperas de un superaño electoral que, en realidad, se adelanta con los comicios de noviembre en España. “Honestamente, no tenemos prisa. Los ciudadanos suecos no son el cajero automático de la UE”, ha lanzado el primer ministro sueco, Ulf Kristersson, que aboga por el hachazo al presupuesto, este jueves en Bruselas. “Estamos con una propuesta claramente insuficiente”, ha advertido, por su parte, el presidente español, Pedro Sánchez. items.title: Santé : La « Medleaders association » mobilise les jeunes professionnels de la santé contre le cancer du sein
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – La MedLeaders Association (MLA) a lancé, le jeudi 15 octobre à Lomé, le MLA Health Summit 2026, une rencontre scientifique destinée à mobiliser les jeunes professionnels de la santé autour des enjeux de prévention, de sensibilisation et de dépistage précoce du cancer du sein. La rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de la célébration des dix années d’existence du MLA et d’« Octobre Rose », mois dédié à la sensibilisation au cancer du sein. Cette rencontre est meublée de panels, de conférences scientifiques, d’ateliers, d’expositions et de stands. Des activités de sensibilisation sont également prévues à l’endroit des élèves, des jeunes filles et des femmes. La MLA Health Summit 2026 ambitionne aussi de favoriser les échanges d’expériences et de renforcer les relations professionnelles entre les acteurs du secteur sanitaire, dans l’optique d’une meilleure implication des jeunes dans la lutte contre cette maladie. Intervenant au nom du ministre chargé de la Santé, le professeur Bello Mofou a souligné une grave prolifération de cette maladie chez les femmes. Il a indiqué que le cancer du sein figure parmi les principales causes de mortalité féminine, d’où la nécessité de renforcer les actions de prévention, de sensibilisation et de dépistage précoce. Pour sa part, le professeur Douaguibe, représentant le doyen de la Faculté des sciences de la santé, a insisté sur l’importance de rapprocher les actions de sensibilisation des populations. Il a appelé à intensifier les campagnes d’information dans les maisons, les quartiers et sur les lieux de culte, afin de toucher un public plus large et d’encourager les femmes à s’intéresser davantage à leur santé. La représentante de la MedLeaders Association, Djibare Wake a mis en avant l’engagement de l’association en faveur de la prévention des maladies non transmissibles et de la promotion de la santé. « À travers ce sommet, l’organisation entend offrir un cadre d’échanges scientifiques aux jeunes professionnels de la santé pour réfléchir aux défis liés au cancer du sein et proposer des approches de solutions sur la base d’un diagnostic précoce », a expliqué Mme Djibaré. Créée il y a dix ans, la MedLeaders Association rassemble de jeunes professionnels de la santé autour d’initiatives visant notamment la prévention des maladies non transmissibles et la promotion de la santé. ATOP/IS/HKM

items.title: FILDAK : après sept ans d’absence, Dakar redevient la capitale du livre
items.description: Sept ans. Il aura fallu sept ans pour que la Foire internationale du livre et du matériel didactique de Dakar (FILDAK) retrouve son public. Ce jeudi, au Centre international du commerce extérieur du Sénégal (CICES), le monde du livre s'est retrouvé pour lancer sa 18e édition. La foire se tient jusqu'au 19 octobre. Une soixantaine d'exposants venus de plus de dix pays y participent, avec l'Égypte comme invitée d'honneur. Le thème : « Bibliothèque, transmission et souveraineté ». L'ambition affichée : faire de Dakar « le cœur palpitant du livre ». Si la foire s'était tue pendant sept ans, c'est en grande partie à cause de la Covid-19. Son retour, la ministre en charge de la culture des industries créative et du patrimoine historique, Mame Coumba Diop, l'avait salué dès le 5 octobre, à l'occasion de la présentation de la programmation, comme « un signal fort pour la culture et l'éducation ». Née en 1985, la FILDAK a toujours poursuivi les mêmes objectifs : renforcer les réseaux de diffusion du livre, mettre en relation tous les maillons de la chaîne, créer une solidarité entre les professionnels, promouvoir le livre et le matériel didactique, faire rayonner la culture du Sénégal et de l'Afrique, et défendre la diversité culturelle. À l'ouverture, présidée par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, le gouvernement a réaffirmé sa ligne. « Le gouvernement maintiendra le livre au cœur de sa politique culturelle », a promis le chef du gouvernement, en ajoutant que « la Bibliothèque nationale et la Maison des archives seront réalisées ». Il s'est aussi arrêté sur le thème de l'édition, qu'il voit comme une invitation à une « réflexion profonde » sur la place de la bibliothèque et de la lecture. À ses yeux, une bibliothèque n'est ni un simple bâtiment ni une collection d'ouvrages. Elle traduit la volonté collective de rassembler, d'organiser et de partager les savoirs, les mémoires et l'imaginaire qui fondent une civilisation. Quant à l'Égypte, son choix comme invitée d'honneur n'a rien du hasard. « Mère d'édition de notre espace régional », elle est liée à l'Afrique subsaharienne, et au Sénégal en particulier, par « de profondes continuités culturelles », a rappelé le Premier ministre, évoquant une civilisation millénaire. Pour lui, ce choix traduit un rapprochement scientifique et culturel entre les deux peuples, une amitié ancienne, mais aussi une diplomatie solide. Du côté égyptien, le vice-ministre de la Culture, Oumar Sélim, a rappelé que son pays fut le premier pays africain aux côtés du Sénégal à l'aube de son indépendance. « Par le savoir, les peuples se rapprochent », a-t-il ajouté, citant l'Université Senghor comme témoignage de la solidarité entre les deux peuples. Mamadou Laye DIÈYE
