items.title: Teacher, 30 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
items.description: PESHAWAR: At least 31 people, including 30 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday. Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim initially told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33, including a female teachers and students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher. Later, he said that 30 students students and a female teacher had been killed. According to the official list of casualties shared by LRH, a total of 61 people were brought to the facility, of which 30 were discharged after being treated. Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP A spokesman for Rewscue 1122 said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way. “When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said. Speaking to Geo News , Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded. “Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said. Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement. Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred. A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak. “Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying. A girl who was injured after a school roof collapse receives first aid at a hospital in Peshawar October 15, 2026. —AFP Speaking to Dawn , Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight. “I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said. “When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added. Resident Sohail told AFP “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said. Volunteers and relatives shift the body of a victim, killed after a roof collapsed at a school, into an ambulance outside a hospital in Peshawar on October 15, 2026. —AFP KP governor orders audit Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse. “The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities. In another statement on his X account, the KP governor added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to “identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary”. “We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Kundi wrote. Later, Kundi also attended the funeral prayers of the dead. Speaking to the media, he said that a team had been constituted to probe the incident and the inquiry was underway. “The first step will be to determine who issued the no-objection certificate to the school,” he said. Kundi also announced that the bereaved families would be given Rs1m as compensation while the injured would be given Rs200,000. “A transparent investigation into the incident will be conducted and those responsible will be identified,” he said. Late at night, a notification by the KP Human Resources Department said a fact-finding inquiry committee had been constituted to probe the incident. The committee is headed by Transport Department Secretary Zubair Ahmed and include Chief Engineer Jamshid Ali Khan of the Communication and Works Department. The terms of reference of the committee state that the body will: Conduct a detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the collapse of the classroom roof and establish the sequence of events Examine the structural condition of the building, quality of construction, maintenance history and compliance with applicable building safety requirements Determine the causes of the collapse and identify any negligence, lapses or responsibility on the part of individuals, school management or concerned regulatory authorities Examine the role of the concerned departments and regulatory bodies in ensuring the structural safety of the school building Recommend appropriate action against those found responsible, if any. Recommend practical preventive measures, including arrangements for structural safety inspections of government and private schools, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. “The committee may co-opt any technical expert, including structural engineer considered necessary and shall submit its report to the chief secretary within 7 days,” the notification said. Earlier, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report on Thursday. The committee included: Javid Iqbal, the chairman of the Private Schools Regularity Authority; Muhammad Farooq, the deputy secretary of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department; and a member to be co-opted by a committee. The committee was tasked with probing the incident and ascertaining the facts that led to the roof collapse, unearthing the factors that led to it, suggesting measures to prevent such incidents in the future and making appropriate recommendations. Separately, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed ordered Peshawar CCPO to oversee the rescue operation and directed the traffic police to establish a “green corridor” to ensure uninterrupted movement of ambulances. Rescue and police teams were directed to utilise all available resources, a statement said. “In this hour of grief, KP police stands with the affected families,” the IGP was quoted as saying. Residents and rescue workers gather near an ambulance after a school roof collapse in Peshawar Pakistan on October 15.—Reuters PM Shehbaz takes ‘serious notice’ Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken “serious notice” of the incident, as he offered his condolences to the bereaved families in a post on X. “Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country,” DPM Dar said. He added that “ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount”. “All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.” PM Shehbaz also phone the KP governor according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The prime minister offered condolences to the families of the deceased and directed authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to the injured and all possible assistance to the affected families, the statement said. The prime minister also sought a comprehensive report on the incident. The governor briefed the prime minister on the incident and informed him that the school owner had been arrested and an investigation into the incident had been launched. The prime minister directed that all aspects of the incident be examined and action be taken against those responsible in accordance with the law, the statement added. Condolences President Asif Ali Zardari also expressed “profound shock and grief” over the tragic school incident in a statement on X. “This heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock,” he said, extending his condolences to the families of the children killed. He directed relevant authorities to provide top-notch medical facilities to the injured and extend assistance to the affected families. “In this hour of sorrow, the entire nation shares equally in the grief of the affected families,” he said. President Zardari emphasised the need for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the incident and to ensure that all educational institutions’ buildings were following safety standards. PM Shehbaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the incident, in a statement shared by his office. He extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured, directing that “all possible medical assistance” be provided. PM Shehbaz has also issued instructions to expedite relief operations, the statement said. In a post on X, he said: “My heart is with the families grieving the loss of their children and a teacher in the tragic roof collapse at a school in Peshawar. No parent should have to endure such pain. I extend my deepest condolences and pray for strength for every family affected.” He said that he had directed that the injured receive the best possible care. “We will ensure a thorough investigation into this tragedy and take every necessary step to protect the safety of children in schools across the country,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed grief over the incident. In a post on X, he said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy, adding that the thought of parents sending their children to school in the morning only to receive news of their deaths was heartbreaking. He expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. Bilawal’s sister, MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari, also extended condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured. She said schools must be places of learning and protection, adding that those responsible for ensuring children’s safety must be held accountable. Unicef also expressed its deep sadness over the incident. Unicef representative in Pakistan, Pernille Ironside, said in a statement: “Unicef extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities affected by this devastating incident.” “Our thoughts are also with the injured children; we wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said. Unicef called for urgent action to ensure that all schools, public and private, meet building safety standards and undergo regular safety inspections. “These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in future,” Ironside said. “Every child has the right to learn in a safe environment, where children can learn, grow and thrive, protected from harm. Going to school should never put a child’s life at risk,” she said. People stand near rubble after a school roof collapse in Peshawar, October 15, 2026. —Reuters The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said it was “appalled” by the deaths. “It is important to stress that this was not an accident but a preventable failure, given that police have reportedly attributed the collapse to a weak structure carrying excessive construction,” it said, noting that a similar incident this year had killed 14 children at a tuition centre in Lahore. The commission called for an “independent, time-bound” inquiry with the findings to be made public. It also stressed the need for accountability of the school owner and the regulators “who allowed unsafe buildings to operate”, compensation for the families affected, and mandatory structural audits of all public and private schools. Roof collapse incidents Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. In July, three girls, aged 3 to 13, were killed after a portion of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed and the rubble fell on them. The same month, a child died, and at least five other people were injured after the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood . On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. The incident had come less than two months after four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed. A probe into the DG Khan incident revealed that construction for an extension of the tuition centre’s building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed. Last week, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm. In June, a labourer was killed, and three others were injured when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed in Khawaspur locality of Lalamusa , Gujrat. The same month, two people were injured after the roof of a house collapsed in Lahore’s Nishtar area. In August, a couple was killed, and their daughters were injured after the roof of their house in Shahzad Town , Islamabad, collapsed following three days of heavy rainfall. Additional input from AFP

items.title: Procès d’Algassimou Diallo : la Cour suprême rejette les requêtes de la défense, qui suspend sa participation
items.description: Le procès d’Algassimou Diallo, ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême, poursuivi pour « provocation à la discrimination, à la haine ou à la violence, de la discrimination et association de malfaiteurs » et placé sous mandat de dépôt le jeudi 27 août 2026, s’est poursuivi ce jeudi 15 octobre devant la Cour suprême. L’audience du jour a été essentiellement consacrée à deux questions majeures : la demande de récusation de trois magistrats siégeant au sein des chambres réunies et la requête en annulation de l’ordonnance de renvoi de l’accusé devant cette juridiction. Dès l’ouverture de l’audience, le collectif des avocats de l’ancien magistrat et ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême a soulevé une question relative à la composition de la formation de jugement. Selon la défense, certains magistrats appelés à juger Algassimou Diallo avaient également pris part à la décision autorisant les poursuites contre lui. « Au niveau de la décision prise par le bureau de la Cour suprême, les membres de ce bureau, il y en avait qui étaient membres de la formation en charge de juger monsieur Algassimou Diallo. Nous avons donc estimé que des magistrats qui ont pris part à une décision ayant conduit à l’autorisation de la poursuite de monsieur Algassimou Diallo ne pouvaient pas se retrouver dans la formation qui devait également le juger ». À la suite de cette observation, les avocats de l’accusé ont introduit une demande formelle de récusation visant trois magistrats, dont Ibrahima Sory I Tounkara, Yaya Boiro et Fatou Bongoura. Selon l’avocat, cette demande était formulée « contre les magistrats qui ont pris part à la délibération du bureau de la Cour suprême pour autoriser sa poursuite ». Saisie de cette requête, la Cour suprême s’est retirée pour délibérer. Après plus de trois heures de suspension, elle a repris l’audience et notifié « un arrêt rejetant la récusation de ces différents membres du bureau qui sont également membres de la formation en charge de juger monsieur Algassimou Diallo ». À la suite du rejet de la demande de récusation, le collectif d’avocats a immédiatement introduit une requête en annulation de l’ordonnance renvoyant Algassimou Diallo devant les chambres réunies pour y être jugé des faits qui lui sont reprochés. Au cours des débats, les conseils de l’accusé ont invoqué plusieurs dispositions du Code de procédure pénale, estimant que les droits fondamentaux de leur client n’avaient pas été respectés au cours de l’instruction. « Sur la violation de ses droits substantiels essentiels de défense, notamment l’article 282 du Code de procédure pénale, qui veut que lorsque le juge d’instruction estime qu’il a fini son instruction, avant de prendre l’ordonnance de règlement, mette le dossier de la procédure par l’organe de son greffier à la disposition des avocats de l’inculpé pour une période de trois jours. À l’effet pour ceux-ci, bien entendu, de présenter ou non des observations qui pourraient aller dans le sens d’un non-lieu possible pour la personne inculpée. Sauf que dans le cas de la présente procédure, cette formalité n’a pas été observée, en ce sens que l’instruction d’une affaire qu’on dit être criminelle s’est tenue en deux jours, lundi et mardi. Mercredi matin, qui était je crois le 3 septembre 2026, nous avons été surpris qu’on nous notifie une ordonnance le renvoyant devant les chambres réunies pour être jugé pour les faits pour lesquels il est donc poursuivi », déplore Me Moussa Diallo. Poursuivant son argumentation, l’avocat a insisté sur l’absence du délai qu’il estime légalement requis pour permettre à la défense de formuler ses observations. « Il n’y a pas un délai de trois jours. Donc, nous avons estimé que la violation de cette formalité-là a porté un coût et une grave atteinte aux droits de monsieur Alghassiamou Diallo. Donc, nous avons demandé que l’ordonnance de renvoi soit annulée pour cela en observant les dispositions des articles 396 et 444 du Code de procédure pénale ». La requête en annulation a donné lieu à des échanges particulièrement vifs entre le procureur général près la Cour suprême, Sidy Souleymane N’Diaye, et les avocats de la défense. À l’issue des débats, la Cour s’est de nouveau retirée pour délibérer. À son retour, elle a rendu sa décision en ces termes : « La Cour reçoit la requête » et, au fond, « elle rejette la demande d’annulation parce que mal fondée ». La défense suspend sa participation au procès À la suite de ces décisions, les avocats d’Algassimou Diallo ont exprimé leur désaccord avec la conduite de la procédure. Estimant que leurs requêtes, qu’ils considèrent fondées, ont été systématiquement rejetées, ils ont annoncé leur décision de suspendre leur participation aux audiences. Le collectif a notamment fait part de ses réserves quant aux conditions dans lesquelles la Cour a statué sur la demande de récusation, soulignant la mention de la présence du ministère public lors de la délibération. « On n’a plus de raison à figurer dans une procédure comme ça. Puisque ce n’est pas un procès qu’on veut juste et équitable, nous n’allons pas appartenir à un procès juste pour, disons, faire le figurant dans une procédure. Et ce que nous avons relevé à travers la première décision qui a quand même intrigué plus d’un, c’est que l’arrêt qui a rejeté la demande de récusation porte la mention que la délibération est faite en présence du ministère public, qui se trouve être notre adversaire dans cette procédure. Alors, je me demande est-ce que, dans ces conditions-là, on peut espérer un procès équitable ? À notre entendant, non. Voilà pourquoi le collectif a décidé de suspendre sa participation à ce procès », a conclu Me Moussa Diallo. Pour rappel, dans cette procédure, l’ancien magistrat Algassimou Diallo est assisté par neuf avocats : maîtres Murielle Houindo, Houleymatou Bah, Lancei 3 Doumbouya, Mama Aissata Fofana, Mamady Soufiane Kouyaté, Alpha Amadou DS Bah, Almamy Samory Traoré, Moussa Diallo et Raffi Raja. L’audience a été renvoyée au vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Procès d’Algassimou Diallo : la Cour suprême rejette les requêtes de la défense, qui suspend sa participation est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Kéran : Des acteurs locaux sensibilisés sur le foncier
items.description: Kantè, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Le Comité régional de concertation Etat-secteur privé (CR-CESP) de la Kara a organisé, le jeudi 15 octobre à Kantè, un atelier de sensibilisation et d’échange sur le foncier. La cérémonie a été présidée par le préfet Douti N’Sarma Mabiba en présence de son collègue de Doufelgou, colonel Aziaba Ayi Sessi et du vice-président de la cour d’appel de Kara, Aboudou-Salami Moutaka. Placée sous le thème « Faciliter l’accès à la terre pour les investisseurs et les producteurs locaux », cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du programme d’activités de l’année 2026 du CR-CESP-Kara. L’objectif est d’éclairer les autorités traditionnelles, les chefs des services déconcentrés, les producteurs et investisseurs ainsi que la population sur les procédures et règlementation d’accès au foncier en vigueur. Il s’agit également d’identifier les contraintes relatives à l’accès à la terre en mettant en exergue les rôles et responsabilités des parties prenantes notamment les autorités coutumières et les services techniques de l’Etat dans la sécurisation foncière. Les travaux ont été marqués par une communication sur le cadre juridique régissant le foncier et des échanges sur le partage d’expériences en matière de contentieux foncier. Le préfet Douti a invité ses administrés à s’approprier les procédures d’accès et de sécurisation foncière afin que les incompréhensions soient réduites pour favoriser des relations plus transparentes entre les différents acteurs. Il a souligné que « le développement des collectivités territoriales dépend de la capacité individuelle et collective de chaque citoyen à créer un environnement favorable à l’investissement et à la production tout en respectant les droits et les intérêts de chacun ». ATOP/PAP/BA

items.title: PZ Cussons Ghana promotes hand washing among schoolchildren through Camel campaign
items.description: PZ Cussons Ghana Limited is promoting hand-washing education among schoolchildren, saying habits developed early in life can help prevent infections and improve public health. The company used its Camel brand to educate pupils at Christ the King School on proper hand-washing techniques as part of activities marking Global Handwashing Day. The engagement featured practical demonstrations and interactive sessions aimed at helping pupils understand the importance of washing their hands with soap and making the practice part of their daily routines. Head of Marketing at PZ Cussons Ghana Limited, Bright Anomah, said the focus on children was deliberate, as lessons learnt at an early age could influence their hygiene practices throughout their lives. He said educating pupils on when and how to wash their hands could help protect them from infections while enabling them to share the knowledge with their families and communities. Mr Anomah also called for greater private-sector involvement in public health education, arguing that the responsibility should not rest solely with government. “Public health shouldn’t be the responsibility of the government alone. It is the responsibility of also the private sector and businesses like us, PZ Cussons, to help the country in terms of social development,” he said. He said businesses should complement their commercial activities with initiatives that promote health awareness and support community development. Brand Ambassador for Camel, Matilda Adu Boateng, encouraged consumers to incorporate hand washing into their daily hygiene routines. She highlighted the benefits of Camel Antibacterial Soap, which the company says offers protection against germs, moisturises the skin and helps eliminate odour. “Washing your hand with Camel Antibacterial Soap, it gives you that triple defence, which is killing germs 99.9 per cent, it moisturises your skin, and it eliminates odour,” she said. The product’s advertised germ-killing claim was not independently verified for this report. Pupils who participated in the engagement demonstrated their understanding of the importance of hand washing and identified key moments when the practice is necessary, including before eating and after using the toilet. One pupil said the session had helped them understand how hand washing could protect against germs and infections. “Today I learnt about how hand washing is important and how it saves us from germs and infections. Thank you to Camel Ghana,” the pupil said. This year’s Global Handwashing Day is being marked under the theme “Be a Handwashing Hero,” which encourages individuals, families, schools, communities and businesses to make hand washing with soap a consistent part of everyday life. PZ Cussons said the campaign forms part of its broader efforts to promote hygiene awareness and encourage practices that contribute to healthier communities. The initiative highlights the importance of reinforcing hand-washing lessons beyond special campaigns, so children can practise proper hygiene consistently at school and at home.

items.title: Algérie-Chine : les médicaments innovants au coeur d’un nouveau partenariat
items.description: Pour bénéficier de l'expertise d’un grand groupe chinois dans la production de médicaments innovants et des matières premières entrant dans l’industrie pharmaceutique, l'entreprise algérienne Pharma Invest a conclu un partenariat avec le chinois Yangtze River Pharmaceutical Group (YRPG). La signature a eu lieu ce jeudi 15 octobre au siège du ministère de l’Industrie pharmaceutique à Alger, en présence notamment du ministre Nassim Kouidri et du directeur général du groupe public Saidal. L’Algérien Pharma Invest signe avec le Chinois YRPG L’accord vise à “renforcer la coopération entre les deux parties en matière de transfert d'expertises et de technologies modernes pour la maîtrise de la production de matières premières à usage pharmaceutique”, indique un communiqué du ministère. L'autre objectif du partenariat est d’accompagner Pharma Invest dans “le développement et la fabrication de médicaments innovants, de manière à renforcer les capacités technologiques et industrielles nationales et à contribuer à la promotion de la qualité de la production locale”, ajoute la même source. Vers un partenariat algéro-algerien entre Pharma Invest et Saidal A la même occasion, lit-on dans le communiqué, il a été procédé à la mise au point des grandes lignes pour la conclusion prochaine d'un accord regroupant Saidal et Pharma Invest “en vue d'une coopération dans la fabrication et la distribution de médicaments à forte valeur ajoutée”. Nassim Kouidri, ministre de l’Industrie pharmaceutique, a salué de telles initiatives qui, a-t-il dit, « contribuent à orienter l'industrie pharmaceutique nationale vers la production de médicaments innovants et la maîtrise des technologies de pointe pour la fabrication de matières premières à usage pharmaceutique, renforçant ainsi les capacités nationales en la matière et appuyant le processus de concrétisation de la souveraineté sanitaire ». L’article Algérie-Chine : les médicaments innovants au coeur d’un nouveau partenariat est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 4è session ordinaire de la commune Kéran 3 : L’élaboration du budget primitif 2027 au menu des travaux
items.description: Kantè, 14 oct. (ATOP)- Les travaux de la 4 è session ordinaire de l’exercice 2026 du conseil municipal de la commune Kéran 3 ont été ouverts le mercredi 14 octobre à Pimini, à environ 27 km à l’est de Kantè. Cette quatrième et dernière session ordinaire de l’année sera marquée par des débats sur l’orientation budgétaire, l’élaboration et l’adoption du budget primitif exercice 2027. L’objectif pour les élus locaux est de dresser le bilan des différentes activités menées au cours de l’année et de définir de meilleures orientations pour le compte de l’exercice 2027. Les échanges sur les stratégies de mobilisation des recettes non fiscales notamment les tickets de marché et d’exploitation de céréales ainsi que la location des locaux et mobiliers sont, entre autres, sujets inscrits au programme de la session. Au cours des travaux, les membres des commissions économique, sociale et domaniale auront également à présenter leurs rapports d’activités menées de juillet à septembre derniers. Les conseillers municipaux sauront apprécier quelques décisions prises lors de la session précédente dont la plus importante est relative à l’intensification de la sensibilisation auprès des contribuables sur la redevance des diverses taxes. Le maire de la commune Kéran 3, Fakounafah Batinata a souligné l’importance de redéfinir de nouvelles orientations plus réalistes et ambitieuses afin de répondre efficacement aux besoins essentiels des populations. Le chef de l’exécutif communal a également relevé la nécessité de faire face aux défis en tenant compte de l’amélioration des infrastructures et du renforcement des services sociaux de base. « Nous devrons également prendre en compte tous les autres aspects notamment économiques et environnementaux liés à la promotion de notre économie locale et à la protection de nos ressources naturelles », a précisé le maire. Les chefs traditionnels, les responsables des services déconcentrés, des membres des organisations de la société civile et des différents comités de développement à la base ont aussi assisté à la cérémonie. ATOP/PAP/MG

items.title: Agent judiciaire de l’État, Me Pépé Antoine Lamah : « Nous prenons acte de l’arrêt dans l’affaire Dr Diané »
items.description: Partie civile dans l’affaire opposant le parquet spécial près la CRIEF à Dr Mohamed Diané, ancien ministre de la Défense nationale sous le régime déchu, Me Pépé Antoine Lamah s’est prononcé sur la décision rendue ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026 par la chambre des appels. Selon le représentant de l’Agent judiciaire de l’État, Me Pépé Antoine Lamah, « La cour a reçu l’État guinéen représenté par l’agent judiciaire de l’État en sa constitution de partie civile, déclaré son action bien fondée et lui a alloué la somme globale de 300 milliards de francs guinéens ». « Nous, avocats de l’État guinéen représentés par l’agence judiciaire, nous prenons acte de cet arrêt », a-t-il indiqué, ajoutant : « nous allons rendre compte à qui de droit et nous aviserons ». Il faut préciser que la chambre des appels de la CRIEF a déclaré non coupable l’ancien ministre, présenté comme le gardien du temple du régime Alpha Condé, des faits de détournement de deniers publics. En revanche, il a été reconnu coupable d’enrichissement illicite et de blanchiment de capitaux. Il a été condamné à quatre ans et huit mois de prison, contre cinq ans initialement. Il a également été condamné au paiement d’une amende de 3 milliards de francs guinéens et de 300 milliards de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts au profit de l’État. Elisa Camara L’article Agent judiciaire de l’État, Me Pépé Antoine Lamah : « Nous prenons acte de l’arrêt dans l’affaire Dr Diané » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Me Sidiki Bérété : « Il reste 1 mois et 15 jours au Dr Mohamed Diané pour purger sa peine »
items.description: La chambre des appels de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) a statué, ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026, dans l’affaire opposant le parquet spécial à l’ex-ministre de la Défense nationale du régime déchu, Dr Mohamed Diané. La chambre des appels a déclaré le prévenu non coupable des faits de détournement de deniers publics. En revanche, il a été reconnu coupable d’enrichissement illicite et de blanchiment de capitaux. Il a été condamné à quatre ans et huit mois de prison, contre cinq ans initialement. Il a également été condamné au paiement d’une amende de 3 milliards de francs guinéens et de 300 milliards de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts au profit de l’État. Au sortir de l’audience, l’un des avocats du prévenu, Me Sidiki Bérété, s’est réjoui en ces termes : « On peut dire déjà merci. On est au bout du tunnel par rapport à la peine, mais on va mûrir la décision avec le client, on va se concerter et donner la suite. La peine infligée est 4 ans et 8 mois et il a purgé environ 4 ans et 6 mois de prison et 15 jours, jour pour jour. Parce qu’il a été placé sous mandat de dépôt le 6 avril 2021. Dès lors ça fait 4 ans 6 mois 15 jours. Donc en compilation des délais, le reste théoriquement 1 mois et 15 jours pour purger la peine ». En ce qui concerne les biens, a-t-il ajouté : « il y a d’autres biens qui ont été mis hors cause, les biens qui n’ont pas fait l’objet de déclaration devant la cour constitutionnelle, d’autres sont confisqués. Mais les biens des tiers quand même ont été mis hors de cause. C’est le verre à moitié plein. On va tirer les leçons et répondre au moment opportunité. Pour le moment, ça va, il nous reste quand même théoriquement 1 mois et 15 jours pour la défense, le premier souci, c’est la liberté, tout le reste c’est secondaire. Le moral est au beau fixe. De toutes les façons on garde sa dignité, c’est ça avant tout ». Elisa Camara L’article Me Sidiki Bérété : « Il reste 1 mois et 15 jours au Dr Mohamed Diané pour purger sa peine » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: UEL: Lyon down Crystal Palace 3-2, Sunderland leave it late
items.description: Ligue 1 club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense. Bayer Leverkusen went top of the table with a 4-0 win, while AC Milan strolled to victory by the same scoreline. It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions. Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes when Corentin Tolisso was quickest to react to the dropping ball at a corner to prod the hosts in front. Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage two minutes into first-half injury time as he tucked home Keito Nakamura’s cross at the end of a slick move. A clever set-piece routine allowed Yeremy Pino to halve the deficit for Palace early in the second period. A clever close-range flick by Pavel Sulc then restored the two-goal buffer for Paulo Fonseca’s charges just inside the final quarter hour. Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes on the clock but the home side held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase. In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki’s 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors. The 15th-placed side in Portugal’s second division stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot. Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores. After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner. – Cisse on fire – Bayer Leverkusen sit pretty at the top of the standings as they followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan. Czech striker Patrik Schick was on target twice from the penalty spot in the first half, either side of a Malik Tillman goal, to ensure the points were wrapped up for Carles Martinez’s side before the interval. Ibrahim Maza added a late fourth. AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse. Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim’s men. La Liga’s Real Sociedad followed up their matchday one loss at home to Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Union Saint-Gilloise. Later, Celtic travel to Lisbon to take on Benfica and Celta Vigo host Italian giants Juventus. Bournemouth’s Vitality Stadium will welcome European football for the first time in the Premier League outfit’s history as they welcome Austrians Sturm Graz. AFP The post UEL: Lyon down Crystal Palace 3-2, Sunderland leave it late appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Zio : Des chefs traditionnels entretenus sur la promotion de nouvelles normes sociales
items.description: Tsévié, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Dix chefs de cantons de la préfecture de Zio ont été sensibilisés sur leur rôle et responsabilité dans la promotion de nouvelles normes sociales favorables à l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, le mercredi 14 octobre à Tsévié. A l’actif de l’ONG La Colombe, l’activité se situe dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet « Améliorer les droits et la santé sexuels et reproductifs et la santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et des adolescents et la nutrition en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre ». Le projet bénéficie de l’appui financier de ONU Femmes à travers le fonds Muskoka. L’objectif de la rencontre est de renforcer l’engagement des chefs de cantons dans l’identification, la promotion et la diffusion des nouvelles normes sociales favorables au développement inclusif et à la protection des droits des femmes, des filles et des groupes vulnérables. Il s’agit aussi d’amener ces gardiens des us et coutumes à relayer les informations reçues auprès des chefs de villages et de quartiers pour un changement de comportement. Les participants ont été éclairés sur la définition des normes sociales; la différence entre normes sociales, traditions et pratiques culturelles et l’influence des normes sociales sur les comportements communautaires. L’atelier privilégie une approche participative comprenant des présentations interactives, des travaux de groupe et le partage d’expériences. Pour le préfet de Zio, Gadewa Mawouna, certaines pratiques et normes sociales sont devenues avec le temps, des obstacles à l’épanouissement des femmes, des filles et des personnes vulnérables, ce qui nécessite des actions de changement positif. Le préfet a appelé les chefs de cantons à être les facilitateurs du changement, des relais de sensibilisation et des défenseurs de la dignité de toutes les composantes des communautés. La coordinatrice de l’ONG La Colombe, Mme Akakpo Adjoa et le secrétaire général de la commune de Zio 1, Akakpo Laoutema, ont relevé que les autorités traditionnelles jouent un rôle déterminant dans l’évolution des comportements et des normes sociales au sein des communautés. Toutefois, reconnaissent-ils, la consolidation de ces changements nécessite une implication accrue des chefs traditionnels afin qu’ils puissent identifier les nouvelles normes sociales émergentes dans leurs communautés. ATOP/BBG/MG

items.title: At UNSC, Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reaffirms support for kingdom's security
items.description: WASHINGTON: Pakistan on Thursday strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian and economic infrastructure, reaffirming its support for the kingdom’s security and right to self-defence amid escalating regional tensions. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) debate on the Middle East, Pakistan’s acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said, “These attacks must cease immediately.” He reiterated Islamabad’s support for efforts to secure a peaceful settlement in Yemen. Pakistan also backed the UN special envoy’s efforts to resume dialogue aimed at achieving a comprehensive and lasting peace in Yemen. Saudi Arabia has, in recent days, come under sustained attack, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the deadliest in years, as the war with the Houthis dramatically escalates. Yemen’s civil war reignited in July after a UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle East war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets. The conflict in the country has caused what the UN calls one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises , leaving most of the nation’s population dependent on aid. The Saudi-led coalition has fought the Houthis since 2015 after they seized Yemen’s capital Sanaa and forced out the internationally recognised government from the city, until a UN-brokered ceasefire in 2022. Concern expressed over Gaza In the same session, Pakistan joined the call for halting settler violence in the West Bank and abandoning attempts to annex occupied Palestinian territory. “In the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, settlement expansion, particularly the E1 project , threatens to sever Palestinian territorial contiguity. Settler violence, demolitions, land seizures and forced displacement are entrenching annexation and dismantling the foundations of peace,” Jadoon said. “All settlement activities must cease […]; settler violence must be halted; and accountability ensured.” The E1 plan was greenlit by Israel last year and would further separate east Jerusalem, occupied and annexed by Israel and predominantly inhabited by Palestinians, from the West Bank. Jadoon added that the international support for a two-state solution to the Palestinian issue must be accompanied by concrete measures to preserve Palestine’s territorial integrity and viability. “The two-state solution remains the internationally agreed framework and the indispensable foundation for just and lasting peace,” he said, adding that Resolution 2803, the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, and the New York Declaration provided mutually reinforcing frameworks for advancing that objective. “Pakistan supports their full and good-faith implementation,” he added. He also condemned Israeli incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque and demanded respect for the historical and legal status quo of the holy sites. Regarding Gaza, Pakistan expressed concern over continued ceasefire violations, Palestinian deaths and restrictions on humanitarian access. Jadoon warned that the approaching winter threatened to worsen the suffering of families living amid destruction without adequate shelter or essential services. He called for the Gaza ceasefire to be fully upheld, humanitarian assistance to be delivered unhindered and at scale, and recovery and reconstruction to proceed without delay. Pakistan also stressed the need to support the work of the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees, and demanded the release of withheld Palestinian revenues to enable the Palestinian Authority to fulfil its responsibilities. Jadoon rejected forced displacement and any attempt to fragment Gaza and the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, which he said constituted a single territorial unit. He called for a “credible, time-bound and irreversible” political process to end the Israeli occupation and establish an independent, sovereign, contiguous and viable Palestinian state on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. Jadoon concluded that lasting peace in the Middle East would remain out of reach as long as the occupation continued and the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination remained unfulfilled. “Pakistan remains committed to advancing dialogue and diplomacy in the region to help de-escalate tensions, resolve differences and promote lasting peace and stability,” he said. The Palestinian representative, Deputy Permanent Observer Majed Bamya, said Israel continued to kill Palestinians despite the ceasefire and questioned what he described as unequal international responses to Israeli and Palestinian casualties. “If violence is an impasse, as we are often told, and I believe it is, how can Israeli militarism be justified while Palestinian pacifism is demanded?” he asked. Bamya said Israel had squandered the international sympathy that followed the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023, through the killing of Palestinians, including children, and the destruction of entire multigenerational families. He said more than 1,000 Palestinians had been killed over three years in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, while Israeli settlers and soldiers continued to perpetrate violence. He called for Gaza and the West Bank to be reunited under the Palestinian Authority, with one government, one legal system and one security authority. “We are either sovereign states, equal in rights and duties, sharing security and prosperity, or warring parties forever,” he said, adding that “occupation must end”. France’s ambassador, Jerome Bonnafont, also called for an end to Israeli settlement expansion, warning that the E1 project, settler violence and financial pressure on the Palestinian Authority were fuelling instability. “The unchecked expansion of settlements—including the E1 project—the clear trajectory toward annexation, the systematic and unpunished acts of terror committed by settlers, and the financial strangulation of the Palestinian Authority all fuel instability, including for Israel itself,” he said. Britain echoed the criticism of Israeli settlement policy. Ambassador Sarah MacIntosh demanded an immediate halt to the E1 project, withdrawal of the relevant tender and an end to settlement expansion. “The Government of Israel must ensure compliance with its obligations under international humanitarian law and remove the current restrictions on this critical aid,” she said, referring to humanitarian assistance for Gaza. The United States defended President Donald Trump’s comprehensive Gaza peace plan, endorsed by Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025), saying its success depended on Hamas disarming and relinquishing its weapons. The UN’s acting Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Ramiz Alakbarov, warned that the ceasefire remained extremely fragile, with Israeli military operations continuing to cause Palestinian casualties. Citing Gaza’s Ministry of Health, he reported approximately 1,500 Palestinian fatalities since the ceasefire, including more than 320 children and 140 women. “During my visit to Gaza on Sunday, I witnessed that, for Palestinians living along the Yellow Line, the ceasefire exists in name only,” he said. Alakbarov warned that winter would deepen the humanitarian crisis, with an estimated 950,000 people living in areas at medium or high risk of flooding and more than 4,000 buildings being used as shelters at risk of collapse. He called for the full implementation of the Gaza peace plan, including the disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups, withdrawal of Israeli forces, deployment of the international stabilisation force and transfer of transitional governance responsibilities to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza. He said the ceasefire must become the foundation for genuine recovery and a lasting political settlement, paving the way for two states living side by side.

items.title: Affaire Dr Mohamed Diané : Charles Wright annonce un pourvoi en cassation contre l’arrêt de la CRIEF
items.description: À la suite de la décision de la chambre des appels de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), intervenue ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026 dans l’affaire de l’ex-ministre de la Défense nationale du régime déchu, Dr Mohamed Diané, le parquet spécial est sorti de son silence. Le procureur spécial près la CRIEF, Charles Wright, a annoncé se pourvoir en cassation contre l’arrêt qui a renvoyé le prévenu des fins de la poursuite pour des faits de détournement de deniers publics et a réduit sa peine à quatre ans et huit mois, contre cinq ans initialement. « Contre cette décision, le parquet relève formellement pourvoi contre l’arrêt qui vient d’être rendu par la chambre d’appel de la cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières. Cette décision, ce n’est pas contre la personne du Dr Diané, mais c’est la mauvaise interprétation de droit qui a été faite dans l’analyse du jugement déféré », a déclaré Alphonse Charles Wright. Ces moyens de pourvoi seront développés en bonne et due forme pour que la Cour suprême, qui est la juridiction de droit, puisse statuer sur les moyens de pourvoi à l’effet de remettre la pendule à l’heure, a-t-il assuré. « C’est une procédure, malheureusement, qui a été jugée en première instance où a été reconnu coupable des faits de détournement de deniers publics, d’enrichissement illicite, mais aussi des faits de blanchiment des capitaux. À partir du moment où la juridiction de jugement s’est prononcée sur la responsabilité pénale, on n’est plus maintenant dans le cadre de la présomption, on est plutôt dans le cadre de la responsabilité pénale retenue contre cette personne. C’est tout à fait naturel qu’il exerce les voies de recours, l’histoire de dire qu’il n’est pas d’accord avec la décision qui le concerne ». Le procureur spécial a indiqué que le ministère public, qu’il a la charge de représenter auprès de cette cour, a toujours été respectueux des droits de toutes les personnes poursuivies devant cette juridiction. « Mais, encore une fois de plus, moi je regarde ce peuple de Guinée, je regarde aujourd’hui ces personnes qui sont là en train de faire nos propres procès à travers de propres actes ». Tout en s’indignant en ces termes : « Je ne peux pas comprendre, le Guinéen lambda ne peut pas accepter. Vous connaissez la personnalité du Dr Diané. Quel est cet inspecteur d’État qui pouvait oser un jour de faire un rapport contre le docteur Gani en Guinée ? Dites-le-moi. Qui peut oser, celui qui se faisait appeler le gardien du temple, à dire non au cours de sa gestion ? Il faut diligenter une enquête d’inspection des finances publiques à travers le ministère des Finances, de l’économie, et cetera, pour en faire une pièce à conviction contre celui qui était là comme étant le gardien de la maison. Comment est-ce que sur le plan purement juridique, la loi concernant la gestion de la comptabilité publique est très claire, et il revient à l’ordonnateur des dépenses de justifier l’exécution de ses dépenses, nonobstant l’absence de tout rapport ? Monsieur Diané n’était pas à même aujourd’hui de justifier l’exécution des fonds publics qu’il a eus à manier. Comment peut-on retenir contre lui qu’il n’y a pas de faits de corruption ? Pour le seul fait pour dire tout simplement qu’il n’y a pas de rapport, par voie de conséquence, qu’il n’y a pas de détournement de deniers publics, alors qu’il est établi de façon formelle, je le dis de façon formelle, que messieurs Docteur Diané avaient bel et bien reçu des fonds publics ? Il les a maniés, et il n’a pas pu prouver l’exécution de ça ». En dépit de tout, a-t-il rappelé : « la carotte était déjà cuite, c’est ce qu’on pouvait quand même laisser entrevoir à travers ce que nous venons d’entendre. Nous avons fait produire ici des éléments factuels pour l’époque, 400 et quelques millions comme salaire. On dit non, vous n’étiez pas là au moment où il y avait tous ces débats au niveau du procureur, ces éléments-là ne doivent pas être pris en compte. L’instruction définitive, c’est à toutes les étapes de la procédure devant la cour. Pourquoi ces éléments ont été écartés ? Docteur Diané, il vous a dit en audience qu’à l’époque où il était simple enseignant, j’ai du respect pour ce qu’il porte. Nous respectons la dignité des personnes qui comparaissent par devant la juridiction qu’on appelle CRIEF. Mais nous avons une obligation, aujourd’hui plus que jamais, à continuer à défendre l’intérêt de la société guinéenne à travers la reddition des comptes que chacun de nous est amené à venir justifier ». Plus loin, il a souligné : « Comment peut-on dire que les règles de marché public n’ont pas été violées par le seul motif qu’il y a un procès-verbal de réception ? La loi sur la détection et la répression de la corruption est très claire. Est constitutive de corruption et infraction assimilée le fait même qu’il n’y ait pas eu de respect des règles de procédure du code du marché public est assimilé à la corruption ». Il a toutefois précisé : « si vous dites qu’il n’y a pas eu de détournement, mais vous savez quand même que les règles de marché public quand même ont été violées à’et le juge saisi des faits et juge saisi aussi de toute question soulevée, et le juge après l’appréciation des faits, s’il se rend compte que la qualification juridique retenue au regard des débats et des éléments factuels, il pouvait s’il y avait de la bonne foi, retenir quand même contre Dr Diané ces éléments ». items.title: 30 NDC aspirants file nominations in Upper West as regional election approaches
items.description: Thirty aspirants have filed nomination forms at the Upper West Regional office of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Wa to contest various regional executive positions ahead of the party’s internal election. The filing attracted constituency executives and grassroots members seeking regional leadership roles, with aspirants highlighting grassroots empowerment, party reorganisation and efforts to retain the party’s parliamentary seats in the region. A total of 60 aspirants picked nomination forms, with all applicants expected to undergo vetting on Friday ahead of the regional delegates conference scheduled for next month. Chairmanship contest Among those contesting the regional chairmanship is Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency Chairman Sombawiere Samba, popularly known as Sankara. He faces incumbent chairman Abdul Nasir Saani, who also filed his nomination on Thursday, and businessman Alhassan Aadam Randy. Speaking after filing, Mr Samba highlighted his progression through the party’s ranks, from polling agent and branch chairman to ward chairman, before serving eight years as Deputy Regional Treasurer and becoming constituency chairman. “I started as a grassroots person… If I succeed, everybody who wants to lead the party in the region must start from the grassroots,” he said. He cited his contributions to development in Nadowli-Kaleo, including the provision of 1,400 chairs distributed across 114 polling stations and the initiation of a permanent constituency office project. Mr Samba pledged to extend similar infrastructure development across the region by helping all constituencies acquire furnished offices and securing a permanent regional headquarters for the party. On the NDC’s parliamentary performance in the region, he argued that credit for winning seats should be shared with constituencies, Members of Parliament and branch executives rather than attributed solely to regional executives. Mr Saani, who filed earlier in the day, urged delegates to retain him as regional chairman. Vice-chairmanship and deputy secretary races Daffiama-Bussie-Issa Constituency Chairman and Dean of Constituency Chairmen, Boniface Tienaah, has filed to contest the regional vice-chairmanship. He said his priority would be to support whoever emerged as regional chairman through advice and practical assistance. “As a vice chairman, you don’t really have the direct mandate. The best you can do is to make sure that you give the best ideas to your regional chairman and support him vividly,” Mr Tienaah said. He stressed the need for regional leadership to remain responsive to branch executives to prevent grassroots members from feeling neglected after elections. The contest for Deputy Regional Secretary has attracted Dr Angsongna Banangmwine Claudius, popularly known as Dr ABC, and former Regional Elections and IT Directorate member Cornelius Naasoa Wuobar. Dr Claudius cited his administrative experience as a former two-time president of the Graduate Students’ Associations of Ghana (GRASAG) at the University of Ghana and the University for Development Studies. He pledged to lobby for 44 tertiary scholarships across the region’s 11 constituencies during a four-year term and to modernise party secretariats through improved IT infrastructure, internet access and dedicated office managers. He also called for fair distribution of opportunities and warned against sidelining branch executives in post-election welfare and programme allocations. Mr Wuobar, who resigned from the Regional Elections and IT Directorate to contest, said his experience as a former Deputy Youth Organiser and Constituency Secretary in Nandom had prepared him for the role. He expressed confidence in the NDC’s structures in the Upper West Region and dismissed the New Patriotic Party (NPP) as a threat to the party’s standing. “We are not going to leave an inch for them… We don’t have boys; we have men. Proper men,” he said. “This time we are going to do shoe-to-shoe; we have already dealt with the boot-to-boot,” he added, suggesting that the party was prepared to match its political opponents at every level. One woman files on opening day Gladys Sufuyani was the only woman to file on the opening day, seeking the position of Deputy Regional Women’s Organiser. The regional vetting committee is scheduled to vet all applicants on Friday, ahead of the regional delegates conference next month.

items.title: Acute hunger in Afghanistan reaches highest levels ever recorded: monitor
items.description: Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday. UN agency heads have called for emergency support to stem the crisis, as a separate report details serious human rights violations from public floggings to a new ban on demonstrations. Record acute malnutrition levels for the Aug-Oct period have seen hunger levels grow for millions of Afghans according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a global initiative aimed at informing decisions based on five phases of food security. Economic pressures are straining households nationwide, contributing to more than 32 per cent of the population facing crisis-level acute food insecurity phase three or above, including 3.4m people experiencing emergency phase four conditions. The current deterioration is driven by disease outbreaks and inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene conditions, compounded by sharply reduced access to nutrition services, the report found. The situation is expected to worsen from November to April during the winter lean season, when nearly 19.2m people are projected to face phase three or above, including 5m people in emergency food insecurity conditions. Acute malnutrition is also set to grow significantly, with 4.04m children under the age of five projected to need treatment between January and December 2027. Although improved rainfall and better agricultural production have supported food availability, declining humanitarian assistance is reducing households ability to cope, the report warned. The World Food Programme (WFP) and Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) issued a stark message on Thursday, calling for urgent funding to scale up food assistance, emergency agricultural support and malnutrition prevention and treatment. We still have a window to act, but it is closing fast, WFP country director John Aylieff said. With urgent support, families can get through the winter with dignity. Without it, many will face impossible choices no parent should have to make. FAO representative Richard Trenchard said families need opportunities to earn a dependable living that helps them withstand the next shock and support to get through this winter. Erosion of human rights The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) on Thursday reported the continued erosion of basic human rights across the country between July and September, with women and girls bearing the brunt of restrictions imposed by Taliban authorities. Girls remain barred from formal education beyond grade six. Asked about the ban, a Taliban spokesperson said that problems and considerations had to be taken into account from the perspective of Sharia law. UNAMA documented more than 50 cases related to the hijab, mostly in Herat and Kabul. In one case, a 13-year-old girl was held overnight. Women were also blocked from entering health clinics and markets without a mehram. The mission recorded at least 443 cases and 97 incidents of ill-treatment by virtue and vice inspectors over offences including hijab violations, trimmed beards, skipped prayers and listening to music. While the de facto Supreme Court stopped publicly announcing such cases on its social media account and website in April, UNAMA documented public lashings of 22 men and six women on charges including theft and adultery, and the arrest of 14 former security force members, with at least four others killed. Several outlets were suspended without clear reasons or appeal procedures. A journalist arrested in July 2025 remains in custody without conviction. A new police law, published in August, bans all demonstrations.

items.title: People move to Lagos because things are working — Former lawmaker
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Deputy Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Hon. Kolawole Taiwo, has attributed the state’s growing population and pressure on public infrastructure to its perceived success, saying people continue to move to Lagos because “things are working.” Taiwo, who represented Ajeromi-Ifelodun Constituency and served as Majority Leader in the Assembly, said this on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he discussed why the All Progressives Congress (APC) has continued to govern Lagos since 1999 despite persistent challenges. Explaining why Lagos continues to experience population growth and infrastructure pressure, the former lawmaker said the situation partly reflects the state’s success, which has continued to attract people from different parts of the country. “The problem in Lagos is a result of the success, and when you are successful, there are some things that will happen to you that, if you are not careful, it would look like it is consuming you,” Taiwo said. He further argued that the state’s growing population had increased the pressure on infrastructure and public services, noting that Lagos had grown from about six million people in 1999 to an estimated 20 million today. “What was the population of Lagos in 1999 compared to the population of Lagos now? 20 million. What was the population of Lagos then? It was around than 6 million,” he said. Taiwo argued that people naturally move to places where they believe opportunities and public services are better, adding that Lagos’ appeal had contributed to the pressure on its infrastructure. “Anywhere there is a good thing, people will move there, and that is what is happening; people are moving towards Lagos because things are working,” the former lawmaker added. “We need a place to put our heads, and there is no government in Lagos that did not do one housing project or the other.” The former Deputy Speaker maintained that successive administrations in the state had undertaken housing projects, insisting that Lagos was making progress despite residents’ concerns aboutits development challenges. “Lagos is improving,” he noted. Taiwo also addressed complaints about refuse collection and waste management, arguing that the increased attention being paid to the problem reflected a change in residents’ awareness and willingness to speak up when public services fell short. “The reason why people are complaining more about refuse now is that their consciousness is very high,” he added. “In those days, the refuse situation was worse than this but nobody sees it. But now, if you ever see a small thing that is not working well, you will see somebody who will say something.” The post People move to Lagos because things are working — Former lawmaker appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cinq grands matchs de la semaine : aperçu et pronostics de MELBET
items.description: © MelBet La semaine prochaine nous réserve plusieurs affiches particulièrement intéressantes. Dans cette sélection, MELBET vous présente cinq matchs à ne surtout pas manquer. Real Madrid vs Séville, LaLiga, 18 octobre Après huit journées, le Real Madrid occupe la quatrième place avec 18 points. Séville est cinquième avec 14 unités. Les Madrilènes comptent déjà six points de retard sur Barcelone et n’ont certainement pas envie d’en laisser trois de plus à domicile. D’autant que Séville ne s’est plus imposé au Santiago Bernabéu en LaLiga depuis décembre 2008. Presque 18 ans ! De quoi terminer l’école et entrer à l’université. Gagner à Madrid semble décidément plus compliqué. La saison dernière, le Real avait remporté les deux confrontations : 2-0 à domicile et 1-0 à l’extérieur. Seul bémol : Vinícius a été expulsé lors de la dernière journée face à Villarreal après avoir tiré Nathan Saliba par les cheveux. Son absence pourrait même, qui sait, profiter à l’équipe. Notre pronostic : victoire du Real Madrid à 1,25. Leeds vs Manchester United, Premier League, 18 octobre Après six journées, Leeds occupe la septième place avec 9 points. Manchester United est treizième avec 6 unités. United n’a remporté qu’un seul match. En revanche, l’équipe n’a pas manqué d’alimenter les mèmes. Lors de la dernière journée, les Red Devils menaient face à Tottenham tout en évoluant en supériorité numérique. Mais Solanke a égalisé à la deuxième minute du temps additionnel : 1-1. Conserver l’avantage face à dix joueurs s’est visiblement révélé trop compliqué. Leeds sait aussi contrarier son rival. La saison dernière, le club a pris quatre points face à Manchester United : 1-1 à domicile, puis victoire 2-1 à Old Trafford. Ce succès en avril était d’ailleurs le premier de Leeds en championnat dans ce stade depuis 45 ans. Cette saison en Premier League, Leeds n’a encore jamais perdu à domicile. Manchester United, de son côté, n’a toujours pas gagné à l’extérieur. Notre pronostic : match nul à 3,6. Liverpool vs Villarreal, Ligue des champions, 20 octobre Les quatre précédentes confrontations européennes entre ces deux équipes ont toutes eu lieu en demi-finales : en Ligue Europa 2015/16 et en Ligue des champions 2021/22. Liverpool en a remporté trois, Villarreal une. Score cumulé : 8-3 en faveur des Anglais. À Anfield, les Espagnols n’ont encore jamais marqué : défaite 3-0 en 2016, puis 2-0 en 2022. Les souvenirs de leurs déplacements à Liverpool ne sont donc pas franchement réjouissants. Cette fois, les deux équipes vont s’affronter pour la première fois en phase de ligue. Pour espérer prendre sa revanche, Villarreal devra déjà commencer par trouver le chemin des filets à Anfield. Pour l’instant, nous faisons davantage confiance aux locaux. Notre pronostic : victoire de Liverpool à 1.515. PSG vs Barcelone, Ligue des champions, 20 octobre Le PSG et Barcelone se sont affrontés à 16 reprises en compétitions européennes officielles. Le bilan est parfaitement équilibré : six victoires chacun et quatre matchs nuls. Même le nombre de buts est identique : 29-29. En 2017, le Barça avait gagné 6-1 après s’être incliné 4-0 à Paris. À l’époque, les Catalans étaient entraînés par Luis Enrique. Aujourd’hui, il dirige le PSG. Les Parisiens sont les champions d’Europe en titre. La saison dernière en Ligue des champions, ils avaient battu Barcelone 2-1 malgré une infirmerie bien remplie ! Cette affiche a aussi une dimension personnelle. Ferran Torres a quitté Barcelone pour rejoindre le PSG cet été. Il y a un an, il avait marqué contre les Parisiens. Cette fois, il pourrait trouver le chemin des filets face à son ancien club. C’est l’un des grands matchs de la saison. Impossible de le manquer. Sinon, comment continuer à se dire fan de football ? Notre pronostic : match nul à 4.28. Bayern vs Arsenal, Ligue des champions, 21 octobre Le Bayern a remporté huit de ses 15 confrontations avec Arsenal en Ligue des champions. Différence de buts : 31-18. Entre 2015 et 2017, les Munichois se sont même imposés trois fois de suite sur le score de 5-1. Même pour infliger une correction, on peut varier les plaisirs. Lors de leurs cinq duels à élimination directe, le Bayern s’est toujours qualifié. Le plus récent remonte à 2024. Arsenal a donc suffisamment de raisons de ne pas apprécier les déplacements à Munich. Mais la saison dernière, les Londoniens se sont imposés 3-1 à domicile. Preuve que les lourdes défaites du passé ne sont plus forcément une fatalité. Harry Kane constitue une autre raison de suivre cette affiche. À huit ans, il a passé une année à l’académie d’Arsenal. Les Gunners ont aujourd’hui de quoi le regretter. L’ancien pensionnaire de leur centre de formation tentera une nouvelle fois de marquer face au club londonien. Notre pronostic : victoire du Bayern à 2.15. items.title: Top 5 oldest countries in the world
items.description: Some of the world’s oldest countries have histories stretching back thousands of years, with ancient civilisations that developed early systems of government, writing, trade, religion and law. However, ranking the oldest countries in the world depends on whether age is measured by the emergence of ancient civilisation, the formation of a unified state or continuous sovereignty. Egypt, Iran, China, India and Greece are among the countries with some of the world’s oldest historical roots. Here are five of the oldest countries in the world based on the history of their ancient civilisations and early states. 1. Egypt Egypt is home to one of the world’s oldest civilisations, with the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt traditionally dated to around 3100 BC. Ancient Egyptian civilisation flourished along the River Nile, producing monumental pyramids, hieroglyphic writing and sophisticated systems of administration. Despite centuries of foreign rule, Egypt has retained a strong connection to its ancient heritage. Its capital is Cairo, and the country remains an important cultural and political centre in North Africa and the Middle East. 2. Iran Iran, historically known as Persia, has roots in ancient civilisations dating back thousands of years. The region was home to Elamite societies, with organised political centres emerging during the third millennium BC. The Achaemenid Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC, later became one of the largest empires of the ancient world. Although Iran’s political systems have changed considerably over the centuries, the country has maintained a distinctive Persian cultural and historical identity. Its capital is Tehran. 3. China China has one of the world’s longest recorded histories, with early civilisations developing thousands of years ago. The Xia dynasty is traditionally dated to around 2070 BC, although details of its history remain debated. The Shang dynasty, which emerged around 1600 BC, is supported by archaeological evidence, including inscriptions on oracle bones. China subsequently developed powerful dynasties, extensive administrative systems and influential philosophical traditions. Despite major political changes, its cultural and written historical heritage spans several millennia. Beijing is the country’s capital. 4. India India’s historical roots extend to the Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished in parts of present-day India and Pakistan more than 4,000 years ago. Major urban centres such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro featured organised settlements, drainage systems and extensive trading networks. Later societies developed influential religious, philosophical and political traditions across the Indian subcontinent. India’s modern republic was established in 1950, following independence from British rule in 1947. Its ancient civilisation, however, predates the modern state by thousands of years. New Delhi is India’s capital. 5. Greece Greece has a rich history associated with the Minoan and Mycenaean civilisations, which flourished in the Aegean region during the second millennium BC. Ancient Greece later became known for its contributions to philosophy, mathematics, politics, drama and science. Its influence helped shape many aspects of modern Western thought and institutions. However, the modern Greek state was established in the nineteenth century after a war of independence against Ottoman rule. Greece’s ancient civilisation and the modern country’s founding date therefore represent different historical milestones. Athens is the country’s capital. Vanguard News The post Top 5 oldest countries in the world appeared first on Vanguard News .
