items.title: Martinez apologises for outburst after meeting with Man Utd officials
items.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for publicly criticising the club’s board for a lack of investment in the transfer market following their defeat by Atletico Madrid. The English giants lost 2-0 to Atletico in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League. They are also off to their worst start to a Premier League season for 40 years. Martinez took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad during the transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season to return to Europe’s top competition. United signed three midfielders — Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — for around £150 million ($198 million), but their spending fell far short of some of their Premier League rivals. In a social media post earlier Thursday, Martinez said he had spoken “out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted”, but stopped short of apologising. But having faced criticism for piling pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick following United’s poor start to the season, Martinez met with club officials. – ‘Passionate’ – Afterwards, Martinez issued a fresh statement saying: “Today (Thursday) I met with the club’s leadership and the manager. “It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game. “Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.” The Argentina international’s post-match comments were backed by some fans. But Martinez has been criticised for his own part in United’s sluggish start to the season. He scored an own goal in a 1-1 draw at bottom-of-the-table Fulham last month and was outmuscled by Dominic Solanke as 10-man Tottenham salvaged a point at Old Trafford last weekend. “When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level,” said Martinez. “These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me. “I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.” Pressure is increasing on Carrick just months after he was appointed manager on a permanent basis. Carrick’s men travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday before another Champions League trip, to Italian side Como, on Wednesday. AFP The post Martinez apologises for outburst after meeting with Man Utd officials appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kefas campaign challenges Taraba opposition to unveil manifestos
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The re-election campaign council of Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, has challenged opposition parties and governorship aspirants to present their manifestos and policy alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections, rather than focus on criticism of the incumbent. The Director of Media and Strategic Communications of the campaign council, Hon. Emmanuel Bello, made the call in a statement issued in Jalingo on Thursday. Bello said election campaigns should focus on practical ideas, realistic policy proposals and competing visions for the development of the state, rather than personal attacks and complaints. He accused some opposition figures of making Kefas the central focus of their campaign engagements without adequately explaining what they would do differently if elected. “Election campaigns should be an opportunity for candidates to explain their manifestos, present workable solutions to public concerns, and convince voters why they deserve the mandate to lead. “Unfortunately, much of the opposition’s campaign in Taraba State has been dominated by complaints, accusations and personal attacks rather than clear policy alternatives,” he said. Bello asked opposition candidates to explain their plans for addressing the state’s challenges beyond criticising the incumbent administration. He said their proposals should cover critical sectors, including security, education, healthcare, infrastructure, civil service welfare and youth empowerment. The campaign spokesman also challenged opposition candidates to publish costed policy documents and financing plans outlining how they intended to fund their proposed programmes. “Criticism is easy. Governing requires ideas, priorities and the capacity to deliver. If the opposition believes the present administration has fallen short, they should identify the gaps and offer practical, costed and achievable solutions,” he said. Bello added that the 2027 election should provide an opportunity for candidates to demonstrate their preparedness for governance through clear policies and achievable commitments. “Anger is not a development plan, accusations are not policy alternatives, and slogans cannot replace the hard work of leadership. The 2027 contest should be about who can present the clearest vision and the strongest commitment to delivering results for the people of Taraba State,” he said. He maintained that the Kefas administration would continue to defend its Moving Forward agenda through what he described as achievements across key sectors. Bello urged voters to scrutinise the manifestos, policy proposals and verifiable records of all candidates before making their choices in the 2027 elections. The post Kefas campaign challenges Taraba opposition to unveil manifestos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: What the Falling Leaves Taught Thoreau
items.description: This is an edition of Time-Travel Thursdays, a journey through The Atlantic ’s archives to contextualize the present. Sign up here. Published in the October 1862 issue of The Atlantic , Henry David Thoreau’s essay “Autumnal Tints” arrived in a season of death. The Civil War was well into its second year, and copies of the magazine began reaching readers shortly after the Battle of Antietam, on September 17, a day with the grim distinction of being the single bloodiest of the conflict. Thoreau himself was already gone, having died four months earlier, a casualty not of war but of tuberculosis. Thoreau’s essay makes no connection between the fall and the conditions of fighting, as the poet John Greenleaf Whittier did in “ The Battle Autumn of 1862 ,” in the same issue. Instead, Thoreau’s work is a written version of what he’d initially imagined as a visual book—one in which he would compile the leaves of all the trees around him and follow their progression through the colors, from green to brown. (The magazine included a simple engraving of a scarlet-oak leaf that he had rendered.) He had first drafted “Autumnal Tints” as a lecture in the 1850s, before the war’s start, and delivered a version of it in what would be the final public talk of his life. The event was far from a resounding success—a local newspaper deemed it “dull, commonplace and unsatisfactory”—and making the trip to Waterbury, Connecticut, in the bitter cold of December 1860 had worsened an illness from which Thoreau would never recover. The revised copy that appeared in The Atlantic gave the story new and enduring life. “If I were to live, I should have much to report on Natural History generally,” Thoreau wrote in a March 1862 letter, a few months before his death. As it was, weak and barely able to breathe, he could do little more than adapt some of his lectures into essays for The Atlantic with the help of his sister Sophia. The enterprise marked a reconciliation with the magazine. In 1858, the first installment of his “Chesuncook” essay had appeared in the June issue, minus one beloved sentence about a fallen pine tree: “It is as immortal as I am, and perchance will go to as high a heaven, there to tower above me still.” He was incensed when he found the line unceremoniously axed from the printed copy. “Is this the avowed character of the Atlantic Monthly?” he demanded in a letter to the editor, James Russell Lowell. “I should like an early reply.” No reply, early or late, was forthcoming. Making matters worse, neither was Thoreau’s payment, which he’d already deemed lower than what he deserved. It took two additional letters to secure the $198 he was due. The arrival of James T. Fields as The Atlantic ’s editor in 1861 cleared the way for new contributions from Thoreau. Fields had first printed Walden seven years earlier at his publishing house, and he suggested another collaboration. Thoreau agreed, on much more favorable financial terms than most of the magazine’s other contributors, and on the condition that “no sentiment or sentence be altered or omitted without my consent.” As Thoreau prepared the manuscripts for Fields, he confessed to a friend an inclination to expunge some of the humor from his writing, noting that “I cannot bear the levity I find.” But much levity does remain in “Autumnal Tints.” It is, on the whole, a joyous celebration of the season, and an invitation to “wild delight.” Through his observations, he divined that “man’s spirits should rise as high as Nature’s,—should hang out their flag, and the routine of his life be interrupted by an analogous expression of joy and hilarity.” As he worked through a catalog of trees and plants, he contrasted his own careful appreciation of the natural world around him (“The expression of this grass haunted me for a week”) with the bustle of his neighbors amid the busy occupations of the harvest. Stopping to take in the brilliant hues of the elms lining the Concord Common, he wondered “if there is any answering ripeness in the lives of the men who live beneath them.” Death, however, is never far from “Autumnal Tints.” Keenly aware of his own imminent demise as he revised this manuscript for publication, Thoreau saw his mortality everywhere in the season. Walking on dead leaves in the forest, he imagined the setting as a grand and consecrated cemetery. “They that soared so loftily,” Thoreau wrote of the leaves, “how contentedly they return to dust again, and are laid low, resigned to lie and decay at the foot of the tree, and afford nourishment to new generations of their kind, as well as to flutter on high! They teach us how to die.” Thoreau, still seeking joy on the verge of his own death, had learned the lesson well.

items.title: Stellarix et Sen Startup veulent rapprocher le cloud souverain des jeunes entreprises
items.description: Héberger et sécuriser ses données, payer en monnaie locale, trouver de nouveaux clients : voilà ce que réclament les startups sénégalaises. Le 15 octobre à Dakar, Stellarix et Sen Startup ont voulu y répondre ensemble, autour du cloud et d'une marketplace ouverte aux solutions de l'écosystème. Comment mettre les infrastructures numériques à la portée des entreprises qui innovent au Sénégal ? C'est la question posée le jeudi 15 octobre 2026, au Jardin Keur Mame Charlotte, aux Almadies, lors du Stellarix Business Breakfast. Sur le thème « Cloud • Marketplace • Continuité d'activité », Stellarix, spécialiste de l'hébergement de données et des solutions cloud, a retrouvé Sen Startup, l'association qui fédère les startups du pays. Pour Nafy Diagne, CEO de Stellarix, la rencontre prolonge le lancement de son cloud souverain. « Nous avons lancé un cloud souverain au mois de janvier », a-t-elle rappelé. Reste à le rendre accessible au plus grand nombre, à commencer par les jeunes pousses. D'où l'association avec Sen Startup, qui permet de parler directement à ceux qui innovent. Concrètement, il s'agit de donner aux entreprises les moyens de développer, héberger et faire tourner leurs applications. Nafy Diagne a passé en revue les différents niveaux du cloud, de l'infrastructure aux plateformes, jusqu'aux logiciels. La question des entrepreneurs reste simple : comment accéder à ces outils sans perdre la maîtrise de leurs données ni de leurs dépenses ? La monnaie locale, un détail qui pèse Chez Sen Startup, on voit dans ce rapprochement une réponse aux attentes des membres. « Nos startups ont besoin de solutions souveraines », a affirmé son président, Momar Diop. Il parle d'héberger les données et les applications locales, mais aussi de les protéger. Pour les plus jeunes entreprises, la possibilité de « payer en monnaie locale » compte tout autant, a-t-il ajouté. Le détail n'en est pas un. Une infrastructure disponible ne sert à rien si la startup ne peut pas la payer facilement. En insistant sur ce point, Momar Diop a ramené la souveraineté numérique à une question très concrète : qui peut vraiment s'en servir ? Une marketplace pour vendre, pas seulement pour acheter La démarche ne s'arrête pas à la fourniture de services. Stellarix veut aussi faire une place aux startups sur sa marketplace, une plateforme qui met des solutions à disposition des clients. Nafy Diagne souhaite qu'elles puissent y « mettre leurs solutions aussi à disposition ». Les jeunes pousses y gagneraient un canal de vente supplémentaire, en plus des ressources techniques. Elles deviendraient ainsi à la fois utilisatrices de l'infrastructure et fournisseuses de solutions. Ce lien entre hébergement et commercialisation est l'un des axes de la collaboration. Il suppose de faire se rencontrer les services de Stellarix et les produits de l'écosystème, dans une logique de complémentarité. Momar Diop a insisté sur la méthode : « Cette séance a été une session de co-construction. » Les échanges ont permis d'expliquer à Stellarix ce que les startups attendent, pour que l'offre colle à des entreprises de profils et de niveaux de maturité très différents. Sauvegarde et continuité d'activité Hébergement, sauvegarde des données, continuité d'activité : ces sujets étaient au cœur du programme. La matinée prévoyait une présentation de Stellarix et de sa marketplace, des ateliers, des restitutions, ainsi que des temps de mise en relation et de mini-diagnostic. L'idée était de rapprocher le débat sur la souveraineté numérique des soucis quotidiens des entreprises : sécurité, coûts, disponibilité des services. Le vrai test viendra après le lancement. Il se mesurera à l'usage que les startups feront de ces solutions et aux débouchés qu'elles trouveront sur la marketplace. Nafy Diagne et Momar Diop partagent en tout cas la même attente : une offre qui accompagne les jeunes entreprises, de l'hébergement de leurs applications jusqu'à leur accès au marché. C.G.D

items.title: UPSA launches laptop assembly plant, requiring new students to assemble their own devices
items.description: The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), has taken a major step towards technology-enabled learning with the official launch of its laptop assembly plant at the AFOA ATA Building. The plant, launched on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, is the university’s response to years of student complaints that teaching is too theoretical. “The main idea behind the UPSA laptop assembly plant is not just about assembling laptops but also to expose our students to the basic things they need to know and, ultimately, to equip them with skills to be self-reliant,” management explained at the launch. “We always teach them theoretical frameworks, but complete education requires that students practise what they learn.” The university says IT education at UPSA is being redefined, moving from watching videos about motherboards to actually making them. “Today, our students can walk to the lab and learn how to make motherboards, as well as assemble and dismantle a lot of gadgets,” the university stated. The training also covers software, app development that interacts with hardware, and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI). In what it describes as a first-of-its-kind model for Ghanaian public universities, UPSA announced that, from the next academic year, every newly admitted student will assemble their own laptop. “Once you are admitted to our university, you assemble your own laptop and use it yourself, and pay for it over time,” management said. “We have come up with a very simple and convenient financing stream. You cannot train a student without a laptop. It is like going to school without a book and a pen.” The plant currently produces 1,000 laptops per week, or about 4,000 a month, with the capacity to produce more through overtime work. The first 25 laptops were assembled by students last Saturday after just three days of training. The facility is also equipped with an S-ray machine to detect faults and will provide warranty and after-sales services. The project is a partnership between UPSA and MDIT, alongside two other private investors. The university says it invested no money in the project, contributing student labour as its equity. The consultant and acting chief executive officer of MDIT said UPSA was chosen because of its professionalism. “MDIT partnered with UPSA because, when we talk about professionalism, you cannot go anywhere other than UPSA,” he said. “Our role is not just to bring a product out but to give skills to our students so they can progress from the basics to the intermediate and advanced levels, where they can also conduct their own research and come up with their own designs and working boards before they graduate.” He disclosed that the training would include short courses lasting between one month and one year in advanced AI, AI agent training, and basic and advanced printed circuit board (PCB) and motherboard training. The courses will be open to all students, not just those studying IT, with a minimum entry qualification of the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) or an equivalent senior high school qualification. “Some of them are into marketing, some are into different fields, but it all starts with the interest,” he said. Beyond the classroom As a business university, UPSA says it intends to commercialise its knowledge by serving as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) for Ghanaian businesses seeking to develop their own laptop, mobile phone and tablet brands locally. “The average Ghanaian businessman knows that … I want to create my own brand. Let me go to UPSA and see how UPSA can create a brand for me. I don’t have to travel outside, pay customs duties and all that,” management said. “Our prayer is that we will scale it up and then, if possible, go nationwide.” Management described the launch as Phase One of the project, with Phase Two focusing on engaging the business community.

items.title: UCC sociologist calls for action on gender inequality to end child marriage
items.description: The Head of the Department of Anthropology and Sociology at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), Prof. Georgina Yaa Oduro, has called for action to address gender inequality, warning that it exposes girls to child marriage and threatens their education and prospects. Speaking at an event to mark the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child at Ekon in the Central Region, she said the practice reflected unequal treatment of boys and girls, with girls bearing a disproportionate burden. “Because why is it that a boy child is not being given out into marriage, but it’s a girl child that is being given out into marriage? So, it is genuinely a gendered issue,” she said. Prof. Oduro cautioned against using poverty and vulnerability to justify child marriage, saying the practice could deepen deprivation across generations, particularly when girls are unable to complete their education. “So, if we are not careful and we argue on poverty and vulnerability, we end up compounding the situation, because then we sow and reap the rippling effects of poverty,” she said. She described education as one way to break the cycle, explaining that it equips girls with knowledge and skills that can improve their prospects, including in entrepreneurship. She added that efforts to end child marriage must begin at home, with parents supporting their daughters’ education and protecting their rights. Informal unions are also a concern The celebration was held under the theme, “End Child Marriage and Invest in the Rights of Girls”. The Central Regional Girl Child Coordinator, Priscilla Cristabel Eshun, warned that child marriage extends beyond formal ceremonies to include informal unions in which girls cohabit with boys and men who have the financial means to support them. “We want to end child marriage, which is not necessarily giving your daughter in marriage, formal marriage. But also, the informal marriage, where children are cohabiting with boys and men who have the financial standing,” she said. Ms Eshun urged parents, traditional authorities and other stakeholders to work together to prevent early unions that disrupt girls’ education. Education Director calls for enforcement of community bylaws The Central Regional Director of Education, Dr Juliette Dufie Otami, urged traditional authorities to enforce community bylaws aimed at ending child marriage and protecting girls. Speaking to JoyNews on the sidelines of the event, she said chiefs had considerable influence and should use their authority to ensure that community directives intended to protect children were enforced. “The challenge we throw to the chiefs is that this is the time their bylaws need to work in the communities. Because we notice that they are now relaxed. They have the power to give out whatever instructions they want our children and our parents to follow,” she said. Dr Otami said Ekon was selected to host this year’s celebration because of its high incidence of teenage motherhood and low learning outcomes. She said the Directorate wanted to work with the community rather than blame it, stressing that the challenges could not be addressed by schools alone. She urged parents and guardians to encourage their daughters to remain in school and called on chiefs, elders, religious leaders and other community figures to challenge practices that harm children. She also urged boys to become active partners in respecting and protecting girls. Dr Otami further called on teachers, particularly male teachers, to act as protectors, mentors and role models. She appealed to stakeholders to keep girls in school, report and resist child marriage, support young mothers who wish to return to the classroom, and invest in children’s education and well-being. Call to prioritise girls’ aspirations The event brought together pupils from schools across Cape Coast and Elmina and featured an appeal from the 2026 National Sanitation Diplomat, Nabeeha Erasoung Sulemana Atiah, who urged parents to support girls’ ambitions. “I want to tell every parent to let their girl child have dreams. Let them go to school to the highest levels to become whatever they want, so they can help their families and the nation at large,” she said. The guest of honour, Tufohene of the Ekon Traditional Area, Nana Wiabo Kwamena V, also encouraged parents to take a greater interest in girls’ welfare and education. The event was organised by the Girls Education Unit of the Central Regional Education Service as part of efforts to raise awareness of child marriage and promote girls’ rights. Stakeholders called for coordinated action by parents, traditional authorities, schools and communities to prevent child marriage, address early cohabitation and ensure that girls can continue their education and pursue their aspirations.

items.title: World Sight Day: Abia screens drivers to prevent road crashes
items.description: By Steve Oko The Abia State Eye Health Management Bureau has taken its eye health campaign to a motor park in Umuahia, offering free eye screening to drivers and passengers as part of efforts to prevent avoidable blindness and promote road safety. The Bureau said the intervention was designed to address the risks posed by poor eyesight among motorists, stressing that clear vision was essential for safe driving and the protection of passengers and other road users. The campaign, organised to mark the 2026 World Sight Day, was held at the Prof. Nnenna Oti Bus Terminal, Umuahia, under the theme, “Safe Eyes, Safe Roads, Safe Lives.” Administrator of the Bureau, Dr Betty Emeka Obasi, said the choice of the motor park was deliberate because thousands of commuters pass through the facility daily, making it an ideal location to reach drivers and other members of the public. She urged motorists to take advantage of the free screening to ascertain the condition of their eyes and seek prompt treatment where necessary. “To the drivers here today, I have one request: please take the test. It takes only a few minutes, and it may save your life and the lives of the people who entrust you with their lives,” Obasi said. She advised drivers not to delay obtaining prescribed corrective glasses or treatment, noting that good eyesight was critical for reading road signs, judging distances and speeds, identifying pedestrians at dusk and coping with glare. According to her, regular eye examinations are essential because some eye conditions, including glaucoma, may progress without obvious symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Obasi also called on parents and teachers to ensure that children undergo eye screening, warning that undetected vision problems could affect their learning and development. She cited findings from a national blindness survey indicating that 84 per cent of blindness among adults aged 40 and above was avoidable. The administrator also referenced global estimates showing that 1.1 billion people were living with vision loss in 2020, a figure projected to rise to 1.8 billion by 2050. Giving an account of the Bureau’s activities, Obasi said it had established and was operating 25 eye clinics and vision centres across Abia’s 17 local government areas. She disclosed that the agency had attended to 33,884 patients in just over two years, conducted 31,152 free eye screenings in communities and performed 1,811 eye surgeries, including 304 free cataract operations. The Bureau, she added, had also identified 6,381 cases of glaucoma through its interventions. Obasi attributed the achievements to Governor Alex Otti’s commitment to improving healthcare delivery in the state. Unveiling a vision corridor at the park, Gov. Alex Otti urged commercial drivers to prioritise regular eye examinations, warning that poor eyesight could endanger lives on the road. Otti, represented by his Deputy, Chief Ikechukwu Emetu, said the event was to promote eye health awareness among drivers and commuters. The governor described good eyesight as a professional necessity for drivers and urged them to embrace the Safe Driver Pledge, which promotes routine eye checks, compliance with traffic regulations and responsible driving. Commissioner for Transport, Dr. Chikezie Ukaegbu, said regular eye screening could facilitate early detection of vision problems, timely treatment and reduction in preventable road crashes. His Health counterpart, Prof. Enoch O. Uche, stressed that good vision was vital to protecting lives and improving productivity. The event was organised by the Abia State Eye Health Management Bureau in collaboration with the state ministries of Health and Transport, and the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC). Hundreds of patients received free eye screening at the event. The post World Sight Day: Abia screens drivers to prevent road crashes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LSN questions Ghana’s proposed five-year presidential term and DCE election reforms
items.description: The Law Students’ Network (LSN) has questioned the government’s decision to support extending Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years, while warning that its proposed model for electing District Chief Executives (DCEs) could undermine local democracy by retaining presidential influence over candidate selection. LSN President Abraham Kwaku Gyasi raised the concerns at a roundtable organised by the Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) in Accra on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The discussion examined the Constitution Review Committee’s report, led by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh, and the government’s position on proposed constitutional reforms. In its position paper issued on July 28, 2026, the government accepted the recommendation to amend Article 66(1) of the 1992 Constitution to extend the presidential term to five years, arguing that the additional time would allow governments to implement policies more effectively. The LSN acknowledged that frequent election cycles could encourage short-term decision-making but argued that a longer mandate alone would not resolve governance challenges. It cited institutional inefficiencies, corruption, weak planning and inadequate accountability, insisting that proponents of the change must provide convincing empirical and institutional evidence to justify it. The network also challenged the government’s proposed approach to electing DCEs, which would allow the President to nominate candidates before they are shortlisted for election. It argued that retaining executive influence over who can contest would weaken the purpose of introducing elections at the local level. “Local democracy requires more than allowing citizens to vote among candidates selected through an executive-controlled process,” the network said, citing Article 240 of the Constitution and noting the IEA’s call for open competition in local elections. The LSN further criticised the government’s rejection of proposals to change the appointment process for the Chief Justice and Justices of the Superior Courts, arguing that judicial appointments are closely linked to the constitutional protection of judicial independence under Article 127. It also questioned the government’s alternative to a proposed ban on MPs serving as Ministers, saying the removal of the requirement for a majority of Ministers to be appointed from Parliament would not eliminate concerns about divided loyalties if MPs could still join the Executive. Despite its reservations, the network welcomed the government’s acceptance of other proposed reforms, including the establishment of an Independent Public Emoluments Commission and the abolition of the death penalty. Other panellists at the roundtable included Titus Owusu Darko, Secretary for Innovation and Entrepreneurship of the National Union of Ghana Students, and Sharif Ghali, President of the Ghana Youth Federation. Former Speaker of Parliament and IEA Distinguished Fellow, Rt Hon. Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye, delivered the opening and closing remarks, while Dr William Kofi Osew moderated the discussion.

items.title: AFCON 2027Q: Black Queens Coach to lead Black Stars for Somalia doubleheader with Tanko, Attram as assistants
items.description: Kim Lars Bjorkegren will take charge of the Black Stars for the November international break as the search for a new head coach continues. The Black Queens gaffer will be in charge for the two games against Somalia next month in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Bjorkegren, who served as assistant to the Black Stars for a game, will return to the setup to lead the team as the interim boss for the doubleheader. The Swedish trainer will be assisted by Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram for the two games as Ghana search for their first win of the qualifying series. Ghana lost the opening game of the qualifiers to Côte d’Ivoire before losing to Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium. Bjorkegren will look to steer the Black Stars to victory in the two games which will be played in Ghana. The Swedish trainer will then turn attention to leading the Black Queens in the first phase of the 2027 Women’s World Cup qualifiers playoffs.

items.title: Coup de théâtre à la Cour Suprême : les avocats d’Algassimou décident de boycotter procès
items.description: Nouveau rebondissement dans le procès d’Algassimou Diallo devant la Cour suprême de Guinée. Après le rejet de leur demande de récusation de trois magistrats et de leur requête en annulation de l’ordonnance de renvoi, les avocats de l’ancien magistrat ont décidé de suspendre leur participation à la procédure. À leur sortie de la salle d’audience, ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026, ils ont dénoncé des atteintes aux droits de la défense et exprimé leurs réserves sur l’équité du procès. Le collectif d’avocats chargé de défendre l’ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême a annoncé son retrait après deux décisions défavorables rendues au cours de l’audience. Dès l’ouverture des débats, la défense avait sollicité la récusation de trois magistrats siégeant au sein des Chambres réunies : Ibrahima Sory 1 Tounkara, Hadja Fatou Bangoura et Yaya Boiro. Les avocats estimaient que ces magistrats ne pouvaient prendre part au jugement de leur client, au motif qu’ils auraient participé à la délibération du bureau de la Cour suprême ayant autorisé les poursuites contre lui. Après plusieurs heures de suspension, la Cour a rejeté cette demande. La défense a alors soulevé une seconde exception, portant sur la nullité de l’ordonnance de renvoi d’Algassimou Diallo devant les Chambres réunies. La défense invoque une violation des droits de son client Pour obtenir l’annulation de cette ordonnance, les avocats ont notamment invoqué le non-respect du délai prévu par l’article 282 du Code de procédure pénale. Selon Me Moussa Diallo, la défense n’aurait pas bénéficié des trois jours légaux pour consulter le dossier et présenter ses observations avant le règlement de l’instruction. « Ce texte veut que lorsque le juge d’instruction estime qu’il a fini son instruction, avant de prendre l’ordonnance de règlement, il mette le dossier de la procédure, par l’organe de son greffier, à la disposition des avocats de l’inculpé pour une période de trois jours », a expliqué l’avocat. Il affirme que cette formalité n’a pas été respectée dans le dossier de son client, dont l’instruction se serait déroulée en seulement deux jours. « Mercredi matin, qui était, je crois, le 3 septembre 2026, nous avons été surpris qu’on nous notifie une ordonnance le renvoyant devant les Chambres réunies pour être jugé pour les faits pour lesquels il est poursuivi », a-t-il déclaré. Estimant que cette situation portait atteinte aux droits de la défense, les avocats ont demandé l’annulation de l’ordonnance de renvoi, en se fondant notamment sur les articles 396 et 444 du Code de procédure pénale. Le ministère public s’est opposé à cette demande. Le procureur général près la Cour suprême, Sidy Souleymane N’Diaye, a soutenu que la procédure devant les Chambres réunies obéissait à des règles particulières et a demandé que la requête soit déclarée irrecevable. Après les débats, la Cour s’est retirée pour délibérer. À son retour, elle a déclaré la requête recevable, mais l’a rejetée au fond, la jugeant mal fondée. « Nous n’allons pas participer à un procès pour faire de la figuration » Cette décision a suscité la colère des avocats. Face à la presse, Me Moussa Diallo a regretté que la Cour n’ait pas suffisamment motivé, selon lui, son rejet de la demande d’annulation. « Lorsqu’elle est revenue, elle nous dit simplement qu’elle reçoit la requête, et qu’au fond, elle rejette la demande d’annulation parce que mal fondée. C’est tout ce qu’elle a dit, contrairement à la première décision qui, même si elle était contestable, était quand même motivée ; et la Cour s’en est limitée là », a-t-il affirmé. L’avocat estime que les décisions successives défavorables à la défense, conjuguées aux irrégularités qu’elle dénonce depuis le début de la procédure, ne lui permettent plus de poursuivre sa participation au procès dans des conditions satisfaisantes. « Alors, nous avons estimé qu’au regard de la façon dont cette procédure a de tout temps été conduite depuis son entame, au regard du rejet systématique de toutes les demandes que nous avons soumises à la Cour, alors même que ce sont des demandes qui reposent sur, disons, des situations certaines, on n’a plus de raison de figurer dans une procédure comme ça », a-t-il déclaré. Il a ajouté : « Puisque ce n’est pas un procès qu’on veut juste et équitable, nous n’allons pas appartenir à un procès juste pour, disons, faire de la figuration dans une procédure. » La présence du ministère public dans la délibération contestée La défense a également exprimé des réserves sur la mention, dans l’arrêt rejetant la demande de récusation, de la présence du ministère public lors de la délibération. Me Moussa Diallo s’interroge sur la conformité de cette situation avec les exigences d’un procès équitable, le ministère public étant, selon lui, une partie adverse dans cette procédure. « Ce que nous avons relevé à travers la première décision qui a quand même intrigué plus d’un, c’est que l’arrêt qui a rejeté la demande de récusation porte la mention que la délibération est faite en présence du ministère public, qui se trouve être notre adversaire dans cette procédure », a-t-il souligné. L’avocat a ensuite mis en doute les garanties d’impartialité offertes par la procédure. « Alors je me demande : est-ce que dans ces conditions-là, on peut espérer un procès équitable ? À notre entendement, non. Voilà pourquoi le collectif a décidé de suspendre sa participation à ce procès », a-t-il conclu. Ce retrait marque une nouvelle étape dans les tensions entre la défense et la Cour suprême. Il intervient alors que la juridiction poursuit l’examen de l’affaire, sur fond de contestations concernant la régularité de la procédure ayant conduit au renvoi de l’ancien magistrat devant les Chambres réunies. Une affaire liée à la diffusion d’un enregistrement audio Algassimou Diallo est poursuivi pour des faits de « provocation à la discrimination, à la haine ou à la violence pour discrimination et association de malfaiteurs ». Il est en détention préventive depuis le 27 août 2026. L’affaire a éclaté après la diffusion sur les réseaux sociaux d’un enregistrement audio dans lequel l’ancien magistrat est accusé d’avoir tenu des propos à caractère communautariste au cours d’un échange avec Cellou Dalein Diallo, opposant guinéen en exil. À la suite de cette affaire, Algassimou Diallo a été limogé de ses fonctions d’avocat général près la Cour suprême, puis révoqué du corps de la magistrature. Il a ensuite été placé en détention préventive, après un passage par la maison d’arrêt de Coyah, avant son transfert à Macenta. Le retrait annoncé par ses avocats ouvre une nouvelle séquence dans ce procès, marqué par des contestations persistantes sur la régularité de la procédure et les garanties d’un procès équitable. Aux dernières minutes, le juge audiencier de la Cour a décidé de suspendre les débats. L’audience reprendra demain, vendredi 16 octobre, à 10 heures.

items.title: Réseaux sociaux au Niger : l’heure de la responsabilité a sonné…
items.description: En date du 10 septembre 2026, le Conseil des ministres a adopté l’ordonnance n° 2026-48 relative à la presse électronique au Niger. L’avènement de l’internet mobile et la prolifération des réseaux sociaux, notamment WhatsApp, Facebook, X, TikTok, YouTube, Telegram, ont radicalement transformé notre quotidien. Du jour au lendemain, chaque citoyen s’est retrouvé doté d’un pouvoir immense au bout des doigts : celui de s’informer, de s’exprimer et d’influencer. Or, cet outil exceptionnel devrait avant tout être le moteur de notre émancipation intellectuelle et économique. À l’avenir, un manque de vigilance ou de retenue que ce soit par distraction ou par excès de zèle pourra avoir des répercussions immédiates et sérieuses sur notre vie : un simple geste en ligne en cas de non-respect de la loi peut basculer dans l’illégalité. Il est indéniable que certains utilisateurs glissent trop souvent vers un terrain dangereux présentant des risques physiques ou naturels pour la sécurité des personnes. Regardons nos fils d’actualité : entre la désinformation galopante, les rumeurs non vérifiées partagées en un clic et les contenus creux, voire insignifiants, qui consument notre temps, nous nous laissons collectivement divertir au détriment de l’essentiel. À l’heure où notre pays fait face à des défis sécuritaires, éducatifs et économiques majeurs, le gouvernement de la Refondation estime que l’espace numérique national ne peut plus se permettre d’être le théâtre permanent de la division ou de la distraction stérile. Il est donc temps d’opérer une prise de conscience individuelle et collective. Être internaute au Niger ne doit plus simplement signifier consommer des données, des publications, des messages ou de nouvelles qui s’actualisent en temps réel sur un réseau social ou une plateforme. Cela doit signifier bâtir une communauté résiliente, éduquée, informée, critiquée et éclairée. L’accès transparent à l’information et à la bonne culture permet à chacun de prendre des décisions lucides et de ne pas céder à la désinformation ou à la panique. Dès lors, chaque citoyen est investi d’une responsabilité d’intégrité, d’honnêteté et de déontologie. L’adoption de cette nouvelle ordonnance reflète ainsi le climat actuel autour de l’expression en ligne dans notre pays. Le cadre juridique s’est considérablement durci, notamment avec la révision de la loi sur la cybercriminalité. Ce double dispositif réglementaire impose des limites strictes aux professionnels des médias ainsi qu’aux citoyens sur Internet et les réseaux sociaux. Les utilisateurs qui exploitent leurs profils, réels ou fictifs, pour s’attaquer gratuitement à autrui ou porter atteinte à l’ordre public, pour se quereller ou s’amuser, sont désormais appelés à la plus grande retenue. En effet, ces différents textes constituent un moyen légal permettant de contrôler directement l’espace informationnel numérique, qui échappait jusqu’ici en partie aux circuits traditionnels. Ce qui incite particulièrement à la réserve, à la prudence, à la modération et à la discrétion, c’est l’ordonnance n° 2024-28 du 7 juin 2024 modifiant la loi sur la cybercriminalité. Elle réintroduit des peines de prison ferme et de lourdes amendes pour les délits commis par le biais des communications électroniques. De plus, la loi exclut expressément l’octroi de circonstances atténuantes ou d’un sursis pour ces infractions. Il convient de souligner que l’infraction de trouble à l’ordre public s’applique même si les données partagées sont avérées. Ainsi, entre l’encadrement de la presse en ligne et la sévérité de la législation sur la cybercriminalité, l’espace d’expression s’est nettement restreint, obligeant chacun à mesurer scrupuleusement ses propos sur les réseaux sociaux. Par conséquent, chaque citoyen est invité à la modération et à la retenue. Le paysage et le contexte ont totalement changé. Dès lors, c’est presque la fin de la récréation pour certains internautes, toujours prêts à prendre des risques. À partir de maintenant, les espaces numériques, longtemps perçus à tort comme des zones de non-droit, font face à un net durcissement des règles et des contrôles pour garantir la sécurité, l’ordre, la conformité ou la qualité. Veillez à votre tour à en informer vos proches. Qu’Allah nous protège et nous guide à agir avec discernement, de manière appropriée et en pleine conscience dans l’usage de l’Internet et des réseaux sociaux. Qu’Il nous préserve de tout égarement et de tout faux pas. Amen ! Par Moustapha Kadi Oumani L’article Réseaux sociaux au Niger : l’heure de la responsabilité a sonné… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: AMA completes road repairs on Kwame Nkrumah Avenue
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has completed sectional repairs and paving works on a stretch of Kwame Nkrumah Avenue in the Central Business District (CBD) to improve road safety and traffic flow. The Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, inspected the completed works, which cover the U-turn area at Lava and the stretch between the Derby Avenue/Kwame Nkrumah Avenue intersection and the Selwyn Market Street/Kwame Nkrumah Avenue intersection. The rehabilitation followed concerns over severe surface abrasions and potholes along the busy road, which had slowed vehicular movement and posed potential safety risks to pedestrians and other road users. Speaking after the inspection, Mr Allotey described the intervention as an important step towards easing traffic congestion, improving road safety and enhancing mobility within the city’s commercial centre. He also expressed satisfaction with the work undertaken. He stressed the importance of regular road maintenance, noting that improved road conditions were essential to supporting commercial activities, reducing travel delays and ensuring the safety and convenience of road users. Before the works began, the Assembly announced the temporary closure of the affected sections to allow contractors to undertake critical repairs, including paving, to restore the road surface and improve its durability. The completed works are expected to improve traffic flow around the Lava U-turn and adjoining intersections, which serve as important access points for commercial vehicles, traders and other road users operating within the CBD. The AMA has urged motorists and other road users to exercise caution, obey traffic regulations and use the rehabilitated road responsibly to preserve the improvements and protect all road users. Mr Allotey was accompanied on the inspection by the Metropolitan Coordinating Director, Douglas N.K. Annoful, and the Metropolitan Director of Finance, Abeeku Amissah. The intervention forms part of the Assembly’s broader efforts to address infrastructure challenges across the metropolis and create a safer, more accessible environment for businesses and the travelling public.

items.title: Law Students’ Network warns executive dominance could undermine constitutional review
items.description: The Law Students’ Network (LSN) has warned that Ghana’s ongoing constitutional review risks an institutional conflict of interest because the executive arm of government retains significant control over decisions on proposed reforms that could limit its own powers. LSN President Abraham Kwaku Gyasi raised the concern at a roundtable organised by the Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) at its Dialogue Centre in Accra on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The forum examined the Constitution Review Committee’s report, chaired by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh, and the government’s response to its recommendations. In a paper presented at the meeting, the network acknowledged that the government was entitled to assess the committee’s proposals because its report was advisory rather than binding. However, it argued that concerns arise when an institution whose powers are under review also has the dominant role in deciding which restrictions should be implemented. The LSN said this was particularly significant where proposals to limit presidential appointment powers or strengthen independent oversight had been rejected. The network also questioned the government’s plan to introduce two bills to implement the proposed reforms, with one covering non-entrenched provisions and the other addressing entrenched provisions that require a referendum. It warned that rushing the drafting and parliamentary consideration of the bills could limit public scrutiny of contentious changes. “Constitutional reform must not become an exercise in legislative speed at the expense of democratic legitimacy,” the paper stated. The LSN said the process should reflect Article 1(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which vests sovereignty in the people. It also referred to figures cited in an assessment by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), which identified 22 recommendations as fully accepted and 25 as partially accepted out of 147 examined, while acknowledging that the methodology behind the figures remained open to scrutiny. Despite its reservations, the network welcomed the government’s acceptance of several proposed reforms, including the establishment of an Independent Public Emoluments Commission, the abolition of the death penalty and measures aimed at strengthening the independence of certain public institutions. Other panellists at the forum included Titus Owusu Darko of the National Union of Ghana Students and Sharif Ghali of the Ghana Youth Federation. Former Speaker of Parliament and IEA Distinguished Fellow, Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye, delivered the opening and closing remarks, while Dr William Kofi Osew moderated the discussion.

items.title: 2027: Idris urges Nigerians to reject voter apathy, vote buying
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has urged Nigerians to reject voter apathy, vote buying and electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general election, calling for greater participation in the democratic process. Idris said eligible voters had a responsibility to protect democracy by participating peacefully in elections, warning that staying away from the polls, selling votes and resorting to violence could undermine the electoral process. The minister made the call in a statement issued on Thursday by his Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, following the flag-off of the National Orientation Agency’s nationwide grassroots mobilisation campaign for the 2027 general election. The campaign, themed, “Your Vote, Your Voice, Our Future: Say No to Apathy, Vote Buying and Violence. Let’s Build a United Nigeria in 2027,” seeks to promote responsible electoral participation and peaceful elections across the country. “An election is more than a day at the polling unit. It is an opportunity for citizens to decide who represents them and to influence the direction of their communities and country. When eligible voters stay away, sell their votes or resort to violence, the entire democratic process suffers,” Idris said. He said the Federal Government, under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, remained committed to strengthening the democratic process and improving public confidence in elections. According to him, Tinubu signed the Electoral Act 2026 into law, introducing reforms aimed at improving transparency and accountability in the electoral process. Idris commended the Director-General of the NOA, Lanre Issa-Onilu, and the agency’s staff for initiating the campaign, urging them to sustain public engagement nationwide. He said the initiative’s success would depend on collaboration among government institutions, electoral authorities, security agencies, community leaders and citizens. Speaking at the event, Issa-Onilu said the agency would deploy its state directorates across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to mobilise citizens at the grassroots. He said the campaign would use local languages, radio programmes, community dialogues, drama and digital platforms to tackle voter apathy, discourage vote buying and prevent electoral violence. “The National Orientation Agency will take this campaign to communities across the country, engaging Nigerians in languages they understand to promote voter participation, discourage vote buying and electoral violence, and encourage the responsible sharing of verified information,” Issa-Onilu said. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to conducting a credible and inclusive 2027 general election. He urged Nigerians to work with electoral stakeholders to ensure peaceful participation, stressing that the success of the polls would require adequate preparation and collective responsibility. “INEC is committed to conducting a free, fair, transparent, inclusive and credible 2027 General Election. Achieving this requires early preparation, strong collaboration among stakeholders and the active participation of Nigerians,” he said. items.title: Mahama to meet relevant stakeholders over concerns about the new Customs Act
items.description: President John Mahama says he will meet with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry and the Free Zones Authority next week to address concerns from industries operating under the Free Zones scheme over provisions in the new Customs Act. The meeting, which will take place after the Finance Minister returns from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund meetings, is expected to resolve concerns that the new law rolls back some of the incentives enjoyed by businesses operating under the scheme. President Mahama said the government is committed to resolving the concerns and ensuring that industries received the support they needed to grow. He added that the government would meet the relevant institutions next week to discuss the matter. The President gave the assurance during a visit to textile manufacturer DTRT, where he reiterated the government’s commitment to supporting local industries and creating jobs. He said, “I know that there has been some new legislation under the new Customs Act, which the Free Zones industries are complaining about because it has rolled back some of the incentives they received. We are holding a meeting next week, when the Minister of Finance returns from the World Bank and IMF Spring and Autumn Meetings. We are holding a meeting with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry and the Free Zones Board Authority in order to resolve the issues you have complained about” President Mahama also announced plans to invest two billion dollars annually in sectors with the potential to create jobs, including textiles and garments, under the government’s New Economy Programme. He said the textile and garment industry align with the government’s 24-hour economy agenda because of its capacity to provide employment for thousands of people. The President further disclosed that the government would finance the construction of three additional textile factories next year in partnership with the private sector. He said the government would support industries with the right incentives to enable them to expand and create more employment opportunities. President Mahama commended DTRT for its growth, noting that the company has expanded from about 500 employees when he first visited its factory in Accra to more than 6,000 workers, most of them women. He recalled that many of the company’s initial workers were recruited from among head porters and trained with support from the Youth Employment Agency. The President said the company’s expansion demonstrated the potential of the textile and garment industry to create jobs, particularly for women. He also expressed the government’s support for domestic investors, emphasising that local businesses would receive the same attention as other investors. President Mahama said a new DTRT factory under construction was expected to employ 5,000 people per shift and operate across three shifts. He expressed confidence in the project and said he intended to return next year to commission the facility. The President added that the government would subsidise training to reduce the cost of starting operations for businesses and help industries develop the skilled workforce they need.

items.title: CHASS demands a 20% increase in SHS funding and payment of outstanding debts
items.description: The Conference of Heads of Assisted Secondary Schools (CHASS) is urging the government to increase operational funding for senior high schools by 20% and settle outstanding debts owed to regulatory creditors. CHASS President, Rev. Fr. Stephen Owusu Sekyere, said inadequate funding and delays in releasing allocations had made it difficult for school authorities to meet essential expenses, including practical lessons, examinations, food supplies and academic materials. Speaking at the 64th annual CHASS conference in Ho, he called for an urgent review of the allocations to reflect prevailing economic conditions and enable schools to manage their operations effectively. “We appeal to the government to upwardly adjust these allocations to align with current economic conditions. Our standard finances running from 2021 to 2024 remain unpaid and require full settlement to enable schools to clear their long-standing indebtedness to benevolent creditors,” he said. Rev. Fr. Sekyere also appealed for the government to expedite the release of funds and clear outstanding debts that continue to place financial pressure on school administrations. Beyond operational funding, he called for investment in essential school infrastructure, including classroom and dormitory furniture, school buses and utility vehicles. He further urged the government to complete outstanding school projects to improve teaching and learning conditions across senior high schools. On the use of technology in schools, the CHASS President called for restrictions on social media access on government-provided student tablets, arguing that the move would minimise distractions and encourage students to focus on their academic work.

items.title: Institut Pasteur de Tunis | Donia Jerab primée au 8ᵉ Congrès international de nutrition
items.description: Le Prix de la meilleure communication orale du 8ᵉ Congrès international de nutrition a été décerné à Donia Jerab, doctorante au Laboratoire de Génomique Biomédicale et Oncogénétique de l’Institut Pasteur de Tunis, sous la direction du Pr Rym Kefi. Sa communication a porté sur l’association entre le variant rs6923761 (Gly168Ser) du gène GLP1R et le profil métabolique chez des patients tunisiens présentant une obésité et lui permis de remporté ce Prix organisé par l’Association Tunisienne des Sciences de la Nutrition. L'IPT précise que ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre de sa thèse de doctorat consacrée à l’étude nutrigénétique de l’obésité en Tunisie, dans la perspective de développer une approche de nutrition de précision. Cette recherche bénéficie d’une bourse MOBIDOC (projet SWAFY, ANPR) et du financement de l’INNTA. « Félicitations à Donia Jerab pour cette distinction !», a encore commenté l’Institut Pasteur de Tunis. items.title: La DGSN accueille des délégations judiciaires de 24 pays dans son nouveau siège à Rabat
items.description: La Direction Générale de la Sûreté Nationale (DGSN) a organisé une cérémonie d'accueil suivie d'une visite de terrain des différentes installations de son nouveau complexe administratif à Rabat, au profit des présidents de Cours de cassation, procureurs généraux et membres de hautes instances judiciaires représentant 24 pays d'Afrique, d'Europe et du Moyen-Orient. Cette visite a été programmée en marge de la participation de ces hauts magistrats étrangers au congrès international organisé par la Cour de cassation marocaine, en partenariat avec l'Association des Hautes Juridictions de Cassation ayant en partage l'usage du français (AHJUCAF), autour de « Justice et intelligence artificielle : opportunités et risques ». L'initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement de l'ouverture de la DGSN sur son environnement national et international, ainsi que de la présentation des missions de la police marocaine. Elle vise à mettre en lumière les infrastructures de son nouveau pôle administratif ultra-moderne et à valoriser les services rendus par l'appareil sécuritaire aux citoyens et aux institutions judiciaires, en tant qu'acteur central de la chaîne de justice pénale. Au cours de cette tournée, les délégations judiciaires étrangères ont visité le Musée de la Sûreté Nationale, découvrant l'histoire de l'institution sécuritaire marocaine, ses étapes marquantes et son évolution institutionnelle au service de la sécurité de la patrie. La visite a également permis d'exposer les installations opérationnelles vitales du nouveau siège, notamment les salles de commandement et de suivi national par caméras destinées à la sécurisation des grandes métropoles, les salles de gestion de crise, ainsi que le centre de sécurité des installations de la DGSN, illustrant le haut niveau de préparation et l'intégration de technologies de pointe dans la gestion sécuritaire. Outre les espaces de travail quotidien offrant un cadre moderne et intégré, les hôtes de la DGSN ont pu inspecter les centres de gestion des données dotés de systèmes informatiques avancés. La visite s'est achevée par la découverte d'équipements de services intégrés au sein du complexe, tels que le centre sportif et la mosquée, traduisant une vision globale dans la conception de cet édifice. Cette démarche consacre la politique d'ouverture de la DGSN et la présentation concrète du niveau de modernisation atteint par l'appareil sécuritaire national. items.title: Investigation launched after male body found in County Cork
items.description: An investigation has been launched after the body of a man was found in County Cork, Gardaí (Irish police) have said. The body, which has not been identified, was discovered in Ballyellis, Mallow, at about 13:30 local time on Thursday. It is understood that he had injuries to his body, Irish broadcaster RTÉ has reported. His body remains at the scene and is being preserved for forensic examination. RTÉ has also reported that the body was found by people who were on the walkway, which is located on the banks of the River Blackwater. An incident room has been set up at Mallow Garda Station and a post-mortem examination will be arranged, which will assist with determining the course of their investigation.

items.title: Le président Tebboune reçoit le général Salifou Modi : Alger et Niamey renforcent leur coopération sécuritaire…
items.description: Le président de la République algérienne, chef suprême des Forces armées et ministre de la Défense nationale, M. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a reçu en audience, mardi 13 octobre à Alger, le ministre d’État, ministre de la Défense nationale de la République du Niger, le général d’armée Salifou Modi, accompagné d’une forte délégation . L’audience s’est déroulée en présence du général d’armée Saïd Chanegriha, ministre délégué auprès du ministre de la Défense nationale et chef d’état-major de l’Armée nationale populaire ; de M. Brahim Merad, alors ministre d’État chargé de l’Inspection générale des services de l’État et des Collectivités locales, avant sa nomination comme ministre d’État, ministre de l’Intérieur et des Collectivités locales ; ainsi que de M. Ahmed Attaf, ministre d’État, ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Communauté nationale à l’étranger et des Affaires africaines. La rencontre s’inscrit dans le renforcement des relations bilatérales entre l’Algérie et le Niger, deux pays voisins confrontés à des défis communs de sécurité, de stabilité et de gestion des espaces frontaliers. Plus tôt dans la journée, le général Salifou Modi avait également été reçu par le général d’armée Saïd Chanegriha au siège de l’état-major de l’Armée nationale populaire. Les deux parties y ont examiné l’état de la coopération militaire bilatérale et échangé leurs points de vue sur les questions d’intérêt commun. Une dynamique bilatérale consolidée Selon le ministère algérien de la Défense nationale, cette visite traduit la volonté commune des dirigeants des deux pays de consolider les mécanismes de coopération, notamment dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité. Le ministre d’état a Défense nigérien a salué la qualité de la coordination multidimensionnelle entre Alger et Niamey, réaffirmant la détermination de son pays à approfondir la coopération militaire avec l’Algérie. Dans un Sahel marqué par des menaces terroristes, des bandits armés et des trafics transfrontaliers, le rapprochement entre Alger et Niamey revêt une importance stratégique particulière. La coordination entre les deux pays porte sur le renforcement de la sécurité aux frontières, le partage du renseignement et la lutte contre les groupes armés qui exploitent les vastes espaces désertiques et les axes de circulation entre le nord du Niger et le sud de l’Algérie. Cette audience conforte ainsi la trajectoire d’un partenariat stratégique algéro-nigérien, au moment où la stabilité du Sahel demeure au centre des priorités diplomatiques et militaires des deux capitales. items.title: We have been scammed by NDC, government is only doing PR – Abanga Fuseini
items.description: The National Youth Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Abanga Yakubu Fuseini, has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of failing to fulfil its promises to Ghanaian youth, describing the government’s initiatives as public relations exercises. He said the NDC had made several promises, particularly on job creation, but young people were yet to see the expected results. “We have been scammed by the NDC. They are just doing PR,” he said in an interview on Asempa FM’s Ekosii Sen show. Mr Fuseini said the government continued to launch initiatives without adequately addressing youth unemployment, describing the situation as embarrassing given the expectations created during the election campaign. He expressed gratitude to delegates and supporters who voted for him, saying his victory demonstrated that consistency and hard work within the NPP could be rewarded. “I am grateful to all my supporters for voting for me to win. Consistency works in the NPP, so as a youth, if you are working for the party, my advice is that you continue the hard work and your reward will come to you,” he said. Mr Fuseini said his immediate priority as National Youth Organiser was to mobilise young people across the country and work towards securing victory for former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the 2028 general election. He urged NPP youth to become ambassadors for Dr Bawumia by communicating his achievements and outlining what he could offer the country if elected President. “Most of the successful initiatives that are working in this country were championed by the NPP, so we are not intimidated by the NDC,” he said. Mr Fuseini also outlined his plans for the party’s youth wing, saying he intends to intensify grassroots mobilisation and expand the party’s presence across the country during his first 100 days in office. He said he was targeting a strong presence in at least six to seven regions as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structures and prepare for the next general election. “In my first 100 days in office, I want to capture a lot of regions, at least six to seven regions fully. I am actively working day and night,” he said. He added that the support he received from delegates had encouraged him to work harder to meet their expectations. According to him, he had undertaken nearly 84 engagements within his first two weeks in office as part of efforts to connect with party members and advance his mobilisation agenda. Mr Fuseini said he remained committed to strengthening the NPP’s youth wing and ensuring that young people played a central role in the party’s campaign to return to power.

items.title: El difícil aterrizaje en el bolsillo de los hogares de una economía que vuela
items.description: La economía española lleva luciendo en los últimos años un sólido expediente académico, hasta el punto de situarse de forma sistemática entre las primeras de la clase en cada examen al que es sometida por las principales instituciones internacionales. Los indicadores avalan esa evaluación: en un entorno de incertidumbre, el producto interior bruto (PIB) crece por encima del resto de los grandes de Europa, la tasa de paro sigue bajando, el número de trabajadores continúa batiendo récords y las finanzas públicas se mantienen a raya. El malestar, sin embargo, campa en la calle . Literalmente. Los hogares ahora se ven presionados por la subida de los precios de los alimentos, de la energía y sobre todo de la vivienda. La segunda jornada del foro CREO, organizado por Cinco Días y Prisa Media, ha servido para debatir ampliamente sobre los grandes canales por los que deberían circular esas mejoras de la economía hasta llegar a los hogares: las pensiones, los salarios o las ayudas sociales. Y el precio de la vivienda . “Vivienda, vivienda, vivienda”, ha dicho nada más llegar el ministro de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, Pablo Bustinduy. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tamale Teaching Hospital records 44 new breast cancer cases in six months
items.description: Breast cancer continues to dominate the caseload at the oncology unit of the Tamale Teaching Hospital (TTH), with 44 new cases recorded in the first half of the year. A specialist oncology nurse at the facility, Evelyn Osei Amoah, said the figure follows 145 new cases recorded last year, a trend she said points to a steady and worrying increase in the disease in the region. “We see other cases within the unit, but breast cancer cases continue to lead in the unit. For the past five years since we started this major breast cancer campaign, breast cancer has always been leading the clinic. The cases that we are seeing are breast cancer, so yes, breast cancer is there; there is an increase,” she said. Madam Amoah made these comments at an annual breast cancer screening organized by the Brooks Dreams Foundation, a local non-profit that has made October globally recognized as Breast Cancer Awareness Month a focal point for its outreach to women in the Northern Region. The health official said increased public awareness is driving more women to seek screening. “The media is playing a key role in amplifying the awareness, thereby encouraging women to come for screening. More survivors are telling their stories, which is also encouraging more women to come forward for screening.” The screening model, she explained, is designed to link community detection to TTH. “When we notice someone has issues after the screening, we refer the person to the TTH. The person comes and we are the same people there. So when you come, what we have to do is we do a biopsy to confirm and then the person is referred to the oncology department where the right treatment is given to the person.” She added The Founder and Chief Executive of Brooks Dreams Foundation, Hajia Memuna Kaleem, said the organization aimed to screen more than 400 people during this year’s exercise. “Every year we try to improve upon the processes and make it more comfortable for people to undertake the exercise,” she said. “We have enough rooms that can screen 15 people at a time. We have the washrooms, water and all their facilities available to be able to make it comfortable while they wait.” Mrs Kaleem said the foundation also provides financial support for patients whose cases are confirmed and referred to the teaching hospital. “Whatever the outcome is, we are able to support the people,” she said. She acknowledged that myths and traditional beliefs had long hindered early detection efforts, but said sustained community engagement was beginning to shift attitudes. She said the Ibrahim Mahama Global Foundation had partnered with Brooks Dreams Foundation for the past two years to support screening and treatment for women. Founded in 2007, Brooks Dreams Foundation is a non-profit focused on empowering women and youth, particularly girls, through programs in education, livelihood and health.

items.title: Houthis launch deadly attack on presidential palace in Yemen's Aden
items.description: The Houthis launched a deadly missile attack Thursday on the presidential palace in the Yemeni government's interim capital of Aden, as Saudi Arabia blamed Iran for the recent dramatic escalation in the long-running war. The attack hit command centres located inside the Al-Maashiq presidential compound used by government forces and the Saudi-led military coalition that supports them, a Yemeni minister said on condition of anonymity.

items.title: Caicedo calls Chelsea ‘home’, vows to repay Alonso’s faith after injury return
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo has described the Premier League club as his “home” and vowed to continue improving as well as become more of a leader on the pitch under manager Xabi Alonso following his return from injury. The Ecuador international made his first start under Alonso in Chelsea’s 5-1 Premier League victory over Bournemouth on Saturday after recovering from a calf injury that restricted his involvement at the start of the season. Speaking in an interview published on Chelsea’s official website, Caicedo expressed gratitude for the support he has received at Stamford Bridge and said he was determined to justify the trust placed in him by the club’s manager and supporters. “I can say Chelsea is my home, because they treat me like I’ve been here for a long, long time,” Caicedo said. “It’s a special place for me. I want to always give them happiness because I know they did everything for me.” The 24-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Brighton and Hove Albion in 2023, also acknowledged Alonso’s influence on his development, promising to continue working to meet the manager’s expectations. “With Xabi I am going to keep developing, for sure, and show him why he trusts me,” he said. Caicedo made an immediate impact against Bournemouth, helping Chelsea establish control in midfield as they secured a convincing victory at Stamford Bridge. He won a tackle in the build-up to Jordan Henderson’s opening goal before winning possession again in the move that led to Morgan Rogers doubling Chelsea’s advantage. The midfielder was substituted in the 72nd minute after Chelsea had taken a 5-1 lead, receiving a standing ovation from the home supporters. Beyond his performances on the pitch, Caicedo said he wanted to become more vocal as a leader within the Chelsea squad. The midfielder is part of the club’s leadership group but admitted that communicating more with his teammates remains an area he needs to improve. “I think every coach tells me that I can improve talking on the pitch, you know? Because they know that I’m a leader, but it will be better for me if I start talking more with the players,” he said. “I try my best, but it’s not in my nature. So when I’m not able to talk, I just try to show even more.” Caicedo also credited former Chelsea defender Thiago Silva with providing an example of effective leadership during their time together at the club. He described being part of the leadership group as a source of pride for himself and his family, adding that he preferred to lead through his performances and actions. The Ecuadorian also praised Chelsea supporters for their backing, particularly fans in his home country, where the club has expanded its community presence. He said hearing supporters sing his song was an amazing feeling and motivated him to deliver consistently strong performances. Caicedo, who has won major honours with Chelsea, said he was confident he could achieve more success under Alonso as he looks to build on his progress at the club. His return from injury and determination to develop further provide a timely boost for Chelsea as they seek to maintain their momentum in the Premier League. items.title: NSITF boss calls for stronger collaboration to boost workers’ welfare
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Oluwaseun Faleye, has urged stronger collaboration among public service agencies to improve workers’ welfare, boost productivity and strengthen social security. The NSITF MD made the call on Thursday in Abuja while delivering a goodwill message at the Technical Retreat on Presidential Priorities, Ministerial Deliverables and the Performance Management System (PMS). He commended the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment for convening the meeting, describing it as a vital platform for dialogue, coordination and exchange of ideas among agencies with shared institutional responsibilities. “I commend the Ministry for providing this platform for dialogue, coordination and the exchange of ideas, such engagements are important because the effectiveness of public service delivery depends not only on the performance of individual institutions, but also on how well we work together,” he said. Faleye, who was represented at the retreat by his Technical Assistant, Dayo Aloa, noted that the collective responsibility of the Ministry of Labour and NSITF remains the same, “to deliver public value, strengthen institutions and improve the welfare and security of Nigerians.” Speaking on the Fund’s mandate, Faleye explained that the NSITF administers the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS) established under the Employees’ Compensation Act 2010, which provides compensation and support for employees and their dependants in cases of work-related injuries, occupational diseases, disabilities and death. “At the heart of this mandate is a simple but important principle: no worker or family should be left without support when a qualifying workplace incident disrupts their livelihood and future,” he said. He stressed that workers’ welfare is inseparable from national productivity, industrial harmony and sustainable economic development, adding that a worker who feels protected contributes more meaningfully to the workplace. Faleye further stated that the Fund’s role goes beyond claims processing and payment of compensation, but includes sustained engagement with employers and workers, improved awareness of the Scheme, stronger compliance with statutory obligations and commitment to workplace health and safety. “We must remain focused on making the Scheme accessible, responsive, transparent and effective for those entitled to its protection,” he stressed. Emphasizing that no single agency can address all dimensions of workers’ welfare, employment protection, workplace safety and social security alone, the NSITF boss called for reduced duplication, knowledge sharing and more coherent responses to challenges facing Nigerian workers and employers. “I therefore see this meeting as an opportunity to deepen our working relationships, identify practical areas of collaboration and strengthen the alignment between our respective programmes and priorities,” he noted. Looking ahead to 2027, the Managing Director reaffirmed NSITF’s commitment to strengthening implementation of the ECS, improving service delivery, promoting employer compliance and advancing workplace safety. “As we deliberate on our institutional responsibilities and targets, we should remain mindful that the ultimate measure of our success is not merely the activities we undertake, but the tangible improvements our work delivers to the people we serve,” he said. He thanked the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and participating agencies for their contributions to public service delivery and wished the meeting fruitful deliberations that will lead to a more productive and secure Nigeria.
